articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Date, start time, favourites, nominees & how to follow on the BBC
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team tells you all you need to know about the 70th Ballon d'Or Ceremony.
articles.body:
Back for its 70th year, the Ballon d'Or ceremony will once again recognise the best footballing talent in the world.

Run by France Football magazine since 1956, it is widely viewed as the pinnacle of individual prizes for professional footballers worldwide.

As ever, the shortlists of contenders for the biggest awards of the night have been a hot topic of debate among football fans.

When and where is the Ballon D'or ceremony?

The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony will take place at 20:00 GMT on Monday, 26 October, at London's Palladium Theatre.

It is the first time the event will be held in London, a move which Uefa says is to pay tribute to the inaugural winner, England's Stanley Matthews in 1956.

The ceremony is traditionally held in France, and has taken place in Paris' Theatre du Chatelet since 2019.

A dual voting system is used to determine Ballon d'Or winners.

For the men's award, a finalised shortlist of 30 players is decided by a team of journalists from both France Football and L'Equipe newspaper and published a couple of months before the ceremony.

This shortlist is then ranked by 100 journalists from around the world, with their rankings combined to decide the winner.

Jurors are instructed to take three factors into account when ranking players. The Ballon d'Or regulations list the following in order of importance:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character

You can read more about the process, and how it works for the women's award, in our Ballon d'Or voting explainer.

Who are the favourites for the men's prize?

A ceremony that lands in the months following a major tournament always provides extra intrigue - and tournaments don't come more major than the World Cup.

It means that jurors can take international performance into account when ranking the shortlisted players for the men's prize.

With Spain victorious in the 2026 World Cup, it could boost the rankings of the six Spanish internationals on the shortlist.

But outstanding individual performances for club and country, even without a return of silverware for the latter, also puts players like Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland into contention.

England captain Kane scored 73 goals across club and international competitions in the 2025-26 season. While jurors are told to only take the most recent season into account when ranking players, Kane's astonishing 156 goals in 158 games for Bayern Munich since 2023 has lifted him to seventh in the German club's top scorer list. He has led the Bundesliga's scoring charts for three consecutive seasons, as well as being Europe's top overall club goalscorer for 2025-26.

Kane also led his country to their best World Cup finish since they won the tournament in 1966. England won the third-fourth place match to win a bronze medal and he finished fifth top scorer for the tournament.

The teenager has twice won the men's Kopa Trophy for best player under the age of 21, taking the prize at both the 2024 and 2025 awards. Having also placed second in the main rankings in 2025, he is once again up for contention in the both the main prize and under-21 categories. The 19-year-old was a key part of both Spain's World Cup-winning side and Barcelona's La Liga and Spanish Super Cup-winning season, despite missing a number of matches through injury.

Yamal's 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona included eight in the Champions League, putting him ahead of Mbappe as the competition's highest-scoring under-19.

While France fell short of both making the World Cup final and winning the third-place match (losing 6-4 to England), captain Mbappe took home the tournament's Golden Boot after finding the net 10 times, becoming the contest's all-time top scorer in the process.

And despite a lack of silverware for Real Madrid, Mbappe scored 42 goals in 44 appearances for his club across all competitions in 2025-26.

While his years of complete Ballon d'Or dominance may be in the past, Messi has still put his name in the mix for a high ranking after captaining his Argentina side to second place in the World Cup.

Eight goals in the competition put him in second place behind Mbappe on the top scorers list, with both players joint-top for assists with four each.

And with 29 goals in 32 appearances helping Inter Miami to their current second-place position in 2026 (with the most recent season running from February to December), individual and club performance are both still a factor for the footballing legend.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner has had consecutive seasons marred by injury since taking home the trophy. Ruled out for 220 days for Manchester City after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament during the 2024-25 campaign, and a further few months out in the 2025-26 season with knee problems, the Spain captain has not had nearly as much game time as most of his fellow nominees.

However, leading your side to a Word Cup win could carry a fair amount of voting heft with the jurors. Rodri was also named the best player of the tournament. It is unlikely to be enough to seal the main prize, but it has been a positive year for him.

Manchester City's star striker helped guide his country to new footballing heights, scoring seven goals to finish as the tournament's joint-third top scorer as Norway reached their first ever World Cup quarter-finals.

Haaland was also the Premier League's top scorer for the 2025-26 season with 27 goals, amid a total of 38 club goals across all competitions - including becoming the fastest player to reach 50 Champions League goals, taking just 49 games to do so.

Full list of candidates for the men's Ballon d'Or:

Ousmane Dembele (Paris St-Germain/France)

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United/Portugal)

Achraf Hakimi (Paris St-Germain/Morocco)

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (Paris St-Germain/Georgia)

Lautaro Martinez (Inter Milan/Argentina)

Willian Pacho (Paris St-Germain/Ecuador)

Who are the favourites for the women's prize?

With no major international competitions in the women's game during the current voting period, jurors can still look to European qualifying matches as well as club performance when allocating their votes.

The current Ballon d'Or holder Aitana Bonmati has been sidelined with injury for the majority of the season following her win, meaning she will not be able to defend her title for a record fourth time.

When it comes to club and success, it's hard to ask much more of Alexia Putellas than captaining Barcelona to a continental quadruple in 2025-26, winning the Liga F, Cope de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and Champions League.

She became Barcelona's joint-second top scorer of all time after scoring two goals in the Champions League semi-final in May, and earned the player of the tournament award in the process.

The two-time winner could equal her former team-mate Bonmati's record of three awards, having also been a key part of Spain's Nations League-winning side.

The WSL top scorer for a third consecutive season, Khadija shaw appears lightyears ahead of her peers when it comes to goalscoring.

Her 21 league goals - eight goals more than closest rival Alessia Russo - and four assists helped Manchester City to their first title in a decade, topped off with two goals in the FA Cup final to seal the domestic double.

The PFA and FWA women's footballer of the year also remains Jamaica's all-time top goalscorer as she captains them through their 2027 World Cup qualification matches.

Despite two months rules out with injury, Ewa Pajor's strong showing during Barcelona's trophy-laden 2025-26 campaign keep her in contention for this year's Ballon d'Or.

Pajor finished top scorer in the Champions League with 11 goals, leaving her joint-second on the all-time list with former team-mate Putellas. She also scored 16 goals in Liga F to finish second top scorer of the season.

Lyon secured a domestic treble in 2025-26 thanks in no small part to Melchie Dumornay, winning the league title as well as the Coupe de France and Coupe de la Ligue.

The France midfielder scored 22 goals and provided 12 assists overall. Despite losing to quadruple-winning Barcelona in the final, Dumornay scored five Champions League goals and was named in the team of the tournament.

Full list of Ballon d'Or Feminin nominees:

Kerstin Casparij (Manchester City/Netherlands)

Temwa Chawinga (Kansas City Current/Malawi)

Caroline Graham Hansen (Barcelona/Norway)

Alex Greenwood (Manchester City/England)

Vivianne Miedema (Manchester City/Netherlands)

Alexia Putellas (London City Lionesses/Spain)

Lionel Messi holds the record for most men's Ballon d'Or wins, taking home the trophy eight times, and also holding the record for most consecutive wins with four.

Cristiano Ronaldo is in second place overall, with five wins.

The Ballon d'Or Feminin has been running since 2018, with Spain's Aitana Bonmati the player with most wins after being awarded the trophy three times.

Full list of men's winners from the last 30 years:

2025 - Ousmane Dembele (Paris St-Germain/France)

2023 - Lionel Messi (Inter Miami/Argentina)

2022 - Karim Benzema (Real Madrid/France)

2021 - Lionel Messi (Paris St-Germain/Argentina)

2019 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2018 - Luka Modric (Real Madrid/Croatia)

2017 - Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid/Portugal)

2016 - Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid/Portugal)

2015 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2014 - Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid/Portugal)

2013 - Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid/Portugal)

2012 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2011 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2010 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2009 - Lionel Messi (Barcelona/Argentina)

2008 - Cristiano Ronaldo (Manchester United/Portugal)

2006 - Fabio Cannavaro (Real Madrid/Italy)

2004 - Andriy Shevchenko (AC Milan/Ukraine)

2003 - Pavel Nedved (Juventus/Czech Republic)

1998 - Zinedine Zidane (Juventus/France)

1996 - Matthias Sammer (Borussia Dortmund/Germany)

2022 - Alexia Putellas (Spain/Barcelona)

2021 - Alexia Putellas (Spain/Barcelona)

2019 - Megan Rapinoe (USA/Seattle Reign)

While the men's award has been given out for 70 years, additional awards have been added to the ceremony over the years.

There will be 13 awards given out at the ceremony:

Men's and Women's Kopa Trophy (for players under 21 years old)

Men's and Women's Yashin Trophy (for best goalkeeper)

Men's and Women's Gerd Muller Trophy (for best striker)

Men's and Women's Johan Cruyff Trophy (for best coach)

Socrates Award (for humanitarian and societal causes)

A full list of candidates for all categories can be found here .

The BBC Sport website and app will have live text updates from the ceremony all evening, covering every award.

Streaming platform Dazn will be broadcasting the full ceremony for viewers in the UK.

articles.title: Manolo González: “No tengo la percepción de que me juegue el cargo”
articles.standfirst: El técnico perico contentaba de forma contundente a las dudas en relación a su futuro y un posible ‘match ball’
articles.summary: El técnico perico contentaba de forma contundente a las dudas en relación a su futuro y un posible ‘match ball’
articles.body: El Espanyol afronta mañana un partido importante ante el Real Racing para tratar de revertir la mala dinámica de resultados que viene arrastrando el equipo perico en las últimas jornadas. Los cuatro tropiezos consecutivos de los blanquiazules han enturbiado el ambiente y generado algo de nerviosismo entorno al equipo. Manolo González, que ha sido el centro de algunas de las críticas, comparecía este mediodía en rueda de prensa antes de la última sesión de entrenamiento del Espanyol. El técnico perico Kike García y Jofre, las únicas bajas: “Solo están las bajas de Kike García y Jofre Carreras. La convocatoria es la misma que ante el Atlético de Madrid. Los 24 jugadores están disponibles”. No cometer errores que penalicen: “En cuestiones tácticas no diré nada para no dar pistas al rival. En situaciones de juego, sobre todo, en controlar los momentos de partido que habrá. El Racing tiene situaciones de ataque continuadas, que las tenemos que controlar bien. Y en general no tenemos que cometer errores individuales que puedan penalizar el trabajo grupal que haga el equipo”. El Racing, un equipo distinto: “Es un rival que ataca de una manera diferente tanto en posicional como en transición. El Racing a nivel ofensivo pone a mucha gente por delante del balón, en un tramo de campo y tienen cosas buenas en este sentido. Si encontramos las claves de la salida de balón donde queremos y atacamos donde queremos, podemos cogerles y atacarles bien en pocos pases, poniendo el balón donde queremos y escoger los momentos. Si lo sabemos hacer podremos sacar el partido haca adelante”. Una semana importante: “Es importante porque entramos en un la jornada 10 y todo empieza a tener más relevancia a nivel de juego y sensaciones. El equipo tiene mejores sensaciones últimamente, pero no de resultados. Tenemos que volver a coger este ritmo y tengo la sensación que los jugadores en los entrenamientos no tienen presión. A partir de aquí, mi trabajo es seguir mejorando el equipo. Trabajaré hasta el último día de mi contrato a muerte por el Espanyol e intentaré que el club esté por encima de mí. Pase lo que pase quiero que el club gane y esté donde merece. Puedo hacer lo que controlo, trabajar todo lo que puedo y meterle horas”. Falta de picardía: “Es una cosa que hemos analizado y que tenemos que analizar todos, tanto jugadores como cuerpo técnico. Son tres puntos más de diferencia y esto te cambia radicalmente la situación clasificatoria. Málaga, Atlético de Madrid y Real Madrid te cambian radicalmente la visión de la clasificación, pero no hay que mirar hacia atrás, sino al partido del Racing de Santander”. Buscar más influencia de Bryan Zaragoza: “Tenemos que intentar que tenga más influencia en los últimos metros dandole más balones o situaciones. Cuando aparece a nivel ofensivo tiene la capacidad de condicionar al rival y tenemos que aprovecharlo más”. Mejorar ‘el otro fútbol’: “Hay cosas que sabes que pueden pasar. Puedes ir ganando en el 90′ y a partir de ahí sabes que hay cosas no te pueden ocurrir como equipo. Esto lo hemos hablado, pero no creo que sea culpa del jugador. Es el que está en el campo, pero es algo de todos. No me apuntaré nunca un mérito que no tengo porque es una cuestión de grupo. Esto lo tenemos que mejorar, que es el otro fútbol, es decir, no somos un equipo de perder tiempo o dar patadas por dar. No hay que hacerlo, pero en los últimos minutos mejorar, por ejemplo, que no nos generen transiciones”. Situación delicada en la tabla: “Me preocupa mucho, al igual que el primer año que llegué que me preocupó ascender y después mantenerse. Yo estoy preocupado porque quiero ganar y hacemos cosas para tener algún punto más de los que tenemos, a pesar de haber hecho una mala primera parte en Butarque y un partido muy malo contra el Elche. El resto de partidos el equipo los ha competido, pero esto no vale de nada, sino que los puntos que se han escapado no se escapen más”. Sobre su futuro en el banquillo: “Siento que el cargo me lo he jugado desde que estoy aquí. Sabemos la exigencia que tiene el Espanyol, pero realmente no pienso que me juegue el cargo en Santander. Lo que quiero es acabar el contrato y cuando llegue el momento si no tengo que continuar no seguiré, como ha pasado con otras personas. El club está por encima de los que estamos aquí. No tengo la percepción, ni por el vestuario ni el club, de que me juegue el cargo. En lo que puedo controlar tengo que hacerlo lo mejor posible». Un partido importante, pero sin dramatismo: “Una final en la jornada 10… Es un partido importante, como todos, pero catalogo de final un partido que no es reversible, como el del Real Oviedo o una final de la Champions porque no hay margen de maniobra. No es una final ni se va a terminar el mundo, pero queremos hacer un buen partido y ganar”. Mejorar en defensa y hacer un partido completo, clave: “No encajar goles como nos ha pasado. Hacer partidos completos defensivamente y recuperarlo, que lo hemos incidido durante la semana donde están y encontrar las ventajas. También donde ponerlas, que no la tenemos que cagar porque es clave. Si encontramos esto, que a veces al jugador le cae esta seguridad y puedes mecanizar poco en el fútbol, pero decir que estos tres puntos son clave y si podemos tener esto con balón lo conseguiremos”. En sintonía con el vestuario: “Lo tenemos que dar todos, no solo los jugadores. No vendré aquí y les echaré mierda a los jugadores porque no lo creo y he estado al otro lado. He sido jugador muchos años y ningún jugador quiere perder. Lo que me transmite el vestuario es esto y el paso adelante es hacerlo como grupo. Como entrenador hay que ayudarles. Es una cosa general”. Sobre el estado de Javi Puado: “Cuando sea titular lo veréis el día del partido. Tenemos que ver como va cogiendo carga de minutos, pero no solo va de partidos, sino de los entrenamientos continuados después de un año de lesión. Le veo bien y estamos contentos con su evolución y como se ha recuperado. Cada día está mejor y su evolución a nivel físico marcará cuando jugará más minutos”. Sobre los debates sobres su figura: “Es lo que da morbo y vende a nivel general. Entiendo que es así y entiendo cual es mi trabajo. Hay que convivir con eso y no me tiene que molestar. En la actualidad nuestra es lo que da más cancha y es lo que hay. También entiendo que cuando los resultados no son del todo buenos se mira a una dirección. Es una cosa con la que tienes que vivir, no es una cosa que me afecte, pero prefiero el entorno que teníamos cuando éramos quintos, pero para eso hay que ganar”. Sobre la presión con la que conviven: “La presión la tenemos todos los partidos, aunque tuviésemos 10 puntos. No cambia nada en la presión porque está en toda LaLiga. Queremos ganar y dar una buena imagen». No existe un problema con el gol: “Hemos pasado de ‘Roberto Selección’ a Roberto está solo. Tuvimos más problemas ante el Atlético de Madrid por ser el rival que es y en Málaga tuvimos alguna más. Vamos a puntualizar en lo deportivo, no es cuestión de estar solo o no, hay que mejorar. No es el peor año ofensivamente, únicamente no hemos ante el Atlético de Madrid. Si miramos años anteriores, el equipo ha mejorado en ese aspecto”. Fastidiado porque el equipo no gana: “Estoy jodido porque el equipo no gana. Sé cual es mi trabajo, lo que hay, la presión y todo. Tengo que trabajar como un cabrón cada semana, echarle muchas horas, venir aquí y darle vueltas a las cosas mil y una veces. Veo entrenar al equipo y no hay quejas, llegas al partido y llevo mal que tienes para puntuar o ganar y lo llevo mal. Toda mi vida he llevado mal perder, así que tengo que darle la vuelta y conseguirlo”.

articles.title: El PSG - Lyon pasa al lunes... y coincidirá con la gala del Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: Debido a las protestas previstas en la capital gala para este fin de semana
articles.summary: Debido a las protestas previstas en la capital gala para este fin de semana
articles.body: Como ya ocurrió el año pasado, el partido del PSG correspondiente a esta jornada de Ligue 1 coincidirá con la gala del Balón de Oro. El duelo ante el Lyon, que estaba programado para el domingo, se ha aplazado a este lunes 26 por los disturbios previstos en París para este fin de semana. El duelo se ha trasladado del domingo al lunes por la noche a petición de la policía de París, según informó este viernes la Ligue 1 en un comunicado. El duelo se disputará en el Parque de los Príncipes a las 20:30 hora local mientras que la Gala del Balón de Oro está prevista para las 21.00 horas en Londres. Los recursos policiales están al límite en la capital francesa debido a las protestas masivas previstas para este fin de semana. "La LFP ha declarado en un comunicado que toma nota de la orden emitida por la prefectura de policía que prohíbe la celebración del partido entre el París Saint-Germain y el Olympique Lyonnais el domingo", comunicaba la Ligue 1. Según fuentes de diversas agencias, el sábado pasado, 110 manifestaciones reunieron a unas 550.000 personas en todo el país para protestar contra el aumento del coste de la vida y las malas condiciones en los centros educativos de Francia. Para este próximo fin de semana hay nuevas convocatorias. Cabe recordar que la temporada pasada, pese a la coincidencia del partido ante el Marsella, Ousmane Dembélé pudo recoger su primer Balón de Oro. El extremo galo estaba lesionado. En esta ocasión, el propio Ousmane se encuentra tocado tras lesionarse ante el Barcelona... y otro candidato como Kvaratskhelia está también fuera de los terrenos de juego, pero después de sufrir una grave lesión del cruzado hace apenas unos días.

articles.title: Michael Carrick: Man Utd boss gives emotional address, refuses to rule out dropping Bruno Fernandes
articles.summary: Michael Carrick speaks for five uninterrupted minutes at media briefing to outline what Manchester United means to him, then refuses to rule out dropping Bruno Fernandes.
articles.body:
Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick delivered a passionate and emotional address lasting five minutes and 30 seconds as he battles to save his job.

And he refused to rule out dropping skipper Bruno Fernandes for Sunday's Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Instead of taking his seat and answering questions as normal in Friday's scheduled pre-match media conference at Carrington, Carrick said he wanted to start himself.

It was a strategy former boss Sir Alex Ferguson used, although the legendary Scot rarely spoke at such length.

After a run of seven games without a win, culminating in Wednesday's shocking 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, and attacks on the club's hierarchy by defender Lisandro Martinez and then Fernandes' condemnation of his own tactics in Italy, Carrick wanted to reaffirm his view of what United stood for.

"Recently we haven't had a good time, I think that's pretty obvious," he said.

"Wednesday was a bad night, and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable.

"My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, and the supporters, and they can be proud of in the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently. It's important we all recognise that.

"The foundation and values of this football club have been etched for many years. I totally understand and get every single one of them.

"There's a resilience about this football club that runs very deep. I've seen it with my own eyes, I've felt it, I'm know some of the individuals closely who have been a big part of that history.

"Entitlement cannot be at this football club.

"It was based on being humble, having humility, and hard work. We can never lose that, and I won't let us lose that."

Asked about Fernandes and whether he has considered dropping him, a defiant Carrick added: "The most important thing for me is the team, the squad and dynamics in the squad.

"It's about the football club. I'll always do what is best for the football club."

Conte plays down 'unfounded' Man Utd speculation

Should Man Utd boss Carrick drop captain Fernandes?

Have Man Utd become the unmanageable club?

Club sources said on Thursday Fernandes would not have the captaincy taken away or be fined for his post-match observations following the Como defeat.

In a further interview on Wednesday night with Sky Italia, the Portugal international referred to Manchester United's storied history.

"At this club, there's too much focus on what's been done in the past," said Fernandes. "But we're not those people anymore. The club and the players need to understand that.

"Unfortunately for us - especially when it comes to the players - those who join expect to win trophies, win games, and reach the highest level, that's been very difficult at this club in recent years."

Whether Carrick was aware of Fernandes' comments about United's history before he spoke was uncertain.

When asked again if he would take the captaincy away from the 32-year-old midfielder, Carrick repeated: "I will always do what is best for the football club."

He then refused to say whether he had spoken to Fernandes about his conduct, adding: "I don't think this is the time to go into too much detail."

Despite the challenge to his authority, Carrick said the United dressing room was not divided.

"No, it's not," he added. "We just need to get back to doing what we do best."

Carrick also said the club were 'doing everything' to support Fernandes and his family, whose Cheshire home was burgled on Wednesday.

"Thankfully they weren't directly affected even though it is an awful situation."

Carrick named legendary United figures such as Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney and Ferguson as examples of the humility, sacrifice and hard work expected of United players.

That was at odds with his post-match criticism on Wednesday, when he said if you don't run forward or back properly, you will not win games.

Asked how he would persuade his current squad to adhere to the values expected and he demanded, Carrick added: "It's clear as day.

"I'm not telling you anything new. I haven't invented that. That's the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent. That never changes.

"What we look like as a group is my responsibility. That's the privileged position I am in. I'll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry.

"[Wednesday] hurts an awful lot, but that doesn't stop me. That hurt is used as pure motivation and inspiration to want more, expect more and get us going in a different direction."

articles.title: Denying Yamal and Mbappé: Harry Kane wins an 'ominous' honour that historically dooms his Ballon d’Or hopes
articles.summary: Harry Kane's recent victory in the MARCA 100 ranking raises questions about his chances for the Ballon d'Or, as history indicates a concerning pattern for winners of this accolade.
articles.body: This upcoming Monday, October 26, 2026, the footballing universe will pivot on its axis as the Ballon d’Or gala leaves French soil for the first time in its 70-year history. Moving across the English Channel to the historic London Palladium Theatre, treating local audiences to a high-stakes homecoming narrative centered around Bayern Munich’s clinical talisman, Harry Kane. Yet, just as the global media begins its final, deafening build-up to France Football’s definitive decision, a fascinating, quieter verdict has slipped out of Madrid. The Spanish newspaper MARCA just released its localized annual list, "Los 100 de MARCA," crowning Kane at the absolute summit after he narrowly pipped Barcelona’s electric teenage phenom, Lamine Yamal.On its own, a ranking by a single Iberian publication carries little institutional weight. However, the true gravity of this list lies in its exhaustive methodology, relying on a massive, heavy-hitting panel of global football professionals rather than editorial whim. Yet, while their conclusion should serve as a fierce endorsement of Kane's individual brilliance, history signals a far darker subtext. Winning this exhaustive panel vote has historically acted less like a launchpad and more like an ominous curse for players eyeing the actual Ballon d'Or trophy.The 25-point thin marginThe voting margin for this 25-26 edition of the MARCA 100 award was nothing short of microscopic. In the closest and most heavily participated edition since the accolade’s inception in the 2021/22 season, Kane secured the crown with 3,962 points. He barely survived the relentless surge of Yamal, who finished a mere 25 points behind at 3,937, failing to defend his number-one position from the previous 2024/25 campaign. Further down the ladder, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé occupied the third spot with 3,440 points, leading a top-ten packed with elite operators like Rodri, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Lionel Messi, Fabián Ruiz, Michael Olise, Ousmane Dembélé, and Pau Cubarsí. On paper, it is a definitive master list of the world's finest talents, representing a massive consensus among football's most respected minds.But as the sport prepares for Monday night's marquee event, this sudden validation forces us to confront a recurring schism in footballing politics: can a player who wins the hearts of the game's actual practitioners convince the media panel that holds the true keys to footballing immortality?The case for the crown: Kane’s undeniable credentialsDismissing Harry Kane’s top billing as a mere byproduct of a localized Spanish poll ignores the profound weight of his accomplishments over the past 12 months. This victory represents an institutional acknowledgment of an industrial-scale output of pure, unadulterated goal-scoring metrics for Bayern Munich, paired with an irreplaceable tactical gravity for England. Dominating a voting pool this competitive requires a level of sustained excellence that borders on the tyrannical.Between August 2025 and July 2026, Kane hammered home a staggering 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country, an all-competition blitzkrieg that sits in the rarified air of modern footballing history, trailing only Lionel Messi's mythical 82-goal campaign in 2011/12.His club footprint alone redefined modern German footballing standards. Dragging Bayern Munich to a dominant treble consisting of the German Super Cup, German Cup, and the Bundesliga title, Kane’s domestic returns exploded to 61 goals and 7 assists in all competitions, the highest single-season return for a major European club talisman since Cristiano Ronaldo achieved the feat in 2014/15.Clinching his third consecutive Bundesliga Torjägerkanone with 36 league goals alongside the European Golden Boot, the 33-year-old fundamentally altered the tactical landscape of the league. Crucially, this output carried deep into the absolute limits of structural pressure. Kane struck in every single knockout round of the German Cup and the UEFA Champions League, accumulating 13 European goals to earn a definitive place in the Champions League Team of the Year.Far from being a purely club-reliant machine, he seamlessly transferred this clinical tyranny to the international arena. Captaining England to a third-place finish at the World Cup, Kane found the back of the net 6 times in 7 matches, elevating his international legacy to fifth among the all-time leading goalscorers in World Cup history with 14 career goals.Why this poll matters at allIf this specific poll carries any weight, it belongs entirely to the mechanics of the sample size rather than the masthead of a single Madrid sports daily. Over a four-year run, the exercise has avoided pure editorial whim by outsourcing its judgment to a jury of 226 voters, a mix of analysts, international reporters, former players, and active managers who evaluate the sport from the trenches. Emerging at the top of this points system means Kane’s relentless club consistency was validated by the people who build defensive game plans for a living. It is a highly respected peer review, but it is also one structurally predisposed to reward sheer volume and output. The question for Monday is whether this insular consensus possesses any real predictive value when handed over to the broader, narrative-driven world of the international press.The MARCA winner has rarely become the Ballon d’Or winnerThe historical ledger of this award suggests that any celebration in Munich might be premature. Across the four fully completed cycles since its inception, the poll's predictive accuracy rate sits at a meager 25 percent. Out of these four trials, only Karim Benzema in the inaugural 2021/22 season managed to translate a MARCA victory into a Ballon d’Or trophy, courtesy of a Champions League and La Liga double for Real Madrid that made him an undeniable consensus pick.Since then, the two honors have violently split. In the 2022/23 campaign, Erling Haaland smashed historic Premier League goal records to secure a continental treble for Manchester City, rightfully topping MARCA's list, only for the Ballon d'Or panel to hand the golden ball to Lionel Messi, choosing to prioritize the ultimate legacy narrative of Messi dragging Argentina to a historic World Cup victory.The following 2023/24 season saw Vinicius Jr. capture the MARCA crown after a glittering domestic and European run, yet the Ballon d'Or stage belonged to Rodri, whose masterclass in anchoring Manchester City's midfield and leading Spain to a flawless Euros triumph carried more weight with the media.Even Lamine Yamal’s spectacular rise to the top of the 2024/25 MARCA ranking did not translate to the ultimate individual prize, which saw Ousmane Dembélé hoist the trophy after a highly decisive season for club and country. When the broader footballing community agrees on a definitive world number one, the Ballon d'Or journalists routinely decide to write a completely different script.Coaches vs. columnists: The clash of criteriaThis constant divergence is not accidental; it is the natural consequence of structural differences in how these juries evaluate the sport. The MARCA 100 relies on its massive grid of 226 voters, heavily featuring former players and tactical coaches who view football through an operational lens. For an ex-professional or a manager, consistency over a grueling nine-month league campaign, structural reliability, and mechanical efficiency are the traits that command respect. They reward the player who is the most difficult to game-plan against week in and week out, which naturally explains why Kane’s relentless goal return resonated so deeply with this specific panel.The Ballon d'Or operates on an entirely different psychological wavelength. Its voting panel is strictly confined to exactly 100 specialized media journalists, with each representing a top-100 FIFA-ranked nation. Journalists do not look at football like coaches do. They are inherently drawn to romance, legacy-defining international narratives, and explosive, self-contained tournament moments. A magical seven-game run at a World Cup or a European Championship will always carry infinitely more weight for a writer than a consistent four-goal haul against mid-table Bundesliga opposition in November. Crucially, the Ballon d'Or bylaws explicitly state that a player's "Class and Fair Play" serves as a mandatory judging pillar. A player's global marketing appeal, on-field temperament, and narrative arc are openly factored into the equation, areas where a flashy international tournament winner can easily manufactured a subjective advantage over a quiet, club-focused goal machine.Breaking the curse or repeating history?The razor-thin 25-point gap separating Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal is symbolic of the broader philosophical battle lines currently dividing modern football. Kane represents the old guard of ruthless, uncompromising efficiency, while Yamal embodies the dazzling, unpredictable future of the sport. By securing the MARCA 100, Kane has won the ultimate endorsement from the game’s insiders, proving that those who truly understand the pitch value his staggering production above all else.But as the glamorous stage at the London Palladium Theatre awaits on Monday night, the question remains whether the 100 select journalists will honor the cold, hard data of expert consensus, or yield to the romantic, tournament-fueled narrative of Yamal’s generational rise. If history is any indicator, Kane has just won a battle that might have cost him the war.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El Barça completa la segunda emisión de bonos e ingresa un total de 210 millones de euros
articles.standfirst: En verano colocó 105 'kilos' y ahora, la misma cantidad
articles.summary: En verano colocó 105 'kilos' y ahora, la misma cantidad
articles.body: El Barcelona ha anunciado este viernes que ha completado con éxito una nueva emisión de bonos (Media Notes) por un importe nominal de 105 millones de euros, con vencimiento en octubre de 2036. Con esta operación, la entidad azulgrana culmina las dos emisiones autorizadas por la Asamblea de socios compromisarios, que suman un total de 210 kilos. La primera colocación, también por valor de 105 millones, se llevó a cabo el pasado mes de julio. Al igual que sucedió en verano, la nueva emisión ha sido suscrita íntegramente por inversores internacionales en menos de 24 horas. La operación se ha cerrado con un diferencial de 202 puntos básicos, el mismo que se registró en julio de 2026. Además, el interés mostrado por los inversores durante el proceso de comercialización ha permitido adelantar la colocación respecto al calendario inicialmente previsto. Según ha explicado el club en un comunicado, la rapidez con la que se ha completado la operación y el mantenimiento de las condiciones financieras reflejan la respuesta favorable del mercado a esta iniciativa. "La rapidez de la colocación y el mantenimiento del diferencial ponen de manifiesto el respaldo del mercado al Barcelona y la confianza de los inversores en su capacidad para generar ingresos y desarrollar su proyecto a largo plazo", señala la entidad. La finalización de esta segunda emisión supone completar el programa de financiación previsto, con un volumen conjunto de 210 millones de euros y un vencimiento fijado para octubre de 2036. Por otra parte, el Barcelona mantiene la calificación crediticia BBB, con perspectiva estable, otorgada por Morningstar DBRS.

articles.title: Ligue 1: PSG v Lyon at Parc des Princes moved to Monday as Paris prepares for another weekend of protests
articles.summary: Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon at the Parc des Princes is pushed back 24 hours as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests.
articles.body:
Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been pushed back 24 hours to Monday as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests.

The fixture at the Parc des Princes in Paris had been scheduled to kick off at 19:45 GMT on Sunday but will instead take place at 20:30 on Monday.

The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) announced the postponement in a statement , external on Friday after French police prohibited the fixture from taking place on its original date.

French authorities are preparing a major security operation for demonstrations planned for Saturday.

Around 550,000 people took part in demonstrations last Saturday to protest rising fuel prices, education standards and the cost of living, which have escalated after weeks of student protests.

Marches took place in several major French cities, including Paris, backed by unions and student groups, and were marred by some incidents of violence, looting and destruction.

The security challenge is further complicated by Sunday's NFL match between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, an event expected to require a significant police deployment.

The game will be played in Saint-Denis, about 10km from Place de la Bastille, where the protests are expected to begin.

The disruptions have already affected France's domestic football schedule with Toulouse's Ligue 1 home game against Troyes moved from Saturday to Sunday at the request of authorities.

Reigning French and European champions PSG are second in the standings after seven matches, while Lyon lead the table on 14 points, ahead of the holders on goal difference.

The match will also now be played on the same day as the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London.

Injured PSG pair Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 winner, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are among the contenders for the award.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership preview: Form strikers in focus & will Rangers respond?
articles.summary: An analysis of the key Scottish Premiership questions before Saturday and Sunday's fixtures.
articles.body:
The painfully familiar feeling of European disappointment beset Scottish football once again on Thursday.

Domestic matters resume on Saturday with four games and two more on Sunday.

The nights are drawing in, so which teams can lift the sense of gloom?

A Saturday night sojourn to Dens Park ended in minor disappointment for Rangers last weekend, with their 2-1 lead short-lived.

The 2-2 draw maintained a unbeaten run for Derek McInnes' side but brought an end to a sequence of seven straight wins.

The real cost, though, was ground lost on Celtic, who opened up a four-point lead at the top by trouncing Hearts 7-1 on Sunday.

A long seven days later, Rangers are back at home to face promoted St Johnstone for the first time in 21 months with several players suffering from a sickness bug.

The last time the Perth side visited, they were three down by the break and got one back in the second period, continuing a run of Ibrox losses to seven in a row.

However, like Dundee, Saints have started the season well, sitting fifth.

Simo Valakari has managed three times against Rangers as St Johnstone boss and is still looking for his first point.

Achieving such a feat on Saturday would not only bolster that positive start to the season, it would like cause further ripples in the still very early Scottish Premiership title race.

Last weekend showed how the narrative about a manager or team can change with just one victory.

Stephen Robinson was criticised not only for Aberdeen's style of play but for just one victory in seven outings over 90 minutes - with the other being a penalty shootout defeat of Kilmarnock in the League Cup.

Saturday's 3-1 win against St Mirren not only lifted the Northern Irishman's side above the visitors into seventh but also turned the stats around to a more positive three wins and only one defeat in their past six outings, albeit Robinson has yet to fully convince the Pittodrie faithful.

Falkirk, meanwhile, were sitting second bottom with one win in eight outings until Saturday.

Lo and behold, a fine 2-1 win at Hibernian and John McGlynn's side can boast they have lost just once in five games as they move up to ninth.

It also goes to show how an in-form striker can make that vital difference in what are often finely balanced match-ups outside the current top three.

Podcast: Euro review & Scottish Premiership preview

Falkirk's upturn in fortunes has coincided with Jacob Murrell, their 22-year-old summer arrival from DC United, scoring four times in his past five games - three in the latest two.

Kevin Nisbet, too late to earn a Scotland recall, has come to life for Aberdeen, scoring in four of their past five outings.

Bradley Fink, the 23-year-old on loan from Wycombe Wanderers, has scored three in four outings as Dundee have gone three games unbeaten, losing just once in five, to sit fourth in the table.

Lyall Cameron will be looking to add to his two goals in three games as Dundee United seek to extend their four-game unbeaten run at home to Aberdeen, where the Rangers midfielder was on loan last season.

The first goal is vital is often a football mantra - and it certainly seems to be the case in the Premiership this season.

Pacesetters Celtic have spent 64.8% of their game time leading in the Premiership this season.

Third-placed Hearts are second behind Celtic, having spent 45.4% of their season in the lead.

Second-placed Rangers missed a chance to overtake Celtic at the top on Saturday thanks to their draw in Dundee and that appears to be their Achilles heel.

Derek McInnes' side have struggled to finish off the opposition by making their dominance tell and have spent 50.8% of their game time drawing - the highest proportion of any side.

Thursday's defeats for Celtic and Hearts further illustrated Scotland's falling stock on the European stage.

With Celtic, their three defeats in a row in the Europa League is in stark contrast to the beginning of their Premiership defence, with only three points dropped so far.

Hammering last season's runners-up Hearts only re-emphasised how difficult it will be for anyone else to win the league this term.

Struggling Hibernian host Martin O'Neill's side on Sunday, with new Easter Road manager Marink Reedijk having lost his first two games in charge and seeking to halt a run of six Premiership games without a win, during which time there has been just one draw.

The Easter Road outfit, have spent the highest proportion of their match time losing this season (49.7%).

Celtic may be disappointed off the back of Thursday's 2-1 defeat by Celta Vigo, but Hibs have the much more daunting task.

The same is true of Motherwell. Five losses on the bounce have brought a degree of pressure on manager Alfred Johansson after an otherwise bright start to the season.

Visitors Hearts have themselves gone four away from home without a win and have won two in 10 on the road this season in all competitions.

However, the Tynecastle side are seven unbeaten against Well, although three of their four meetings last season were draws and their latest three visits have also ended level.

The big question for Wouter Vrancken's side is, how do they respond to Sunday's heavy defeat at Celtic Park and the 2-0 Conference League loss away to Trabzonspor?

articles.title: Another week, another embarrassing fan-player incident. College football appears to have a problem
articles.summary: After an Alabama fan slapped a Georgia player and a Texas fan flipped the bird in the face of Florida players on consecutive weeks, what's it going to take f...
articles.body:
Listen up, because this is the most important piece of advice you're going to receive as we head into Week 8 of the college football season.

If you find yourself at a stadium and somehow luck into a sideline pass or a premium seating area near the benches or end up in one of those crazy field-rush situations, there is absolutely one thing you must keep in mind.

Don't trash talk them. Don't touch them. Don't flip them the middle finger. And if you somehow do any of those things, understand that cameras are everywhere and there's no place to hide anymore.

What are the odds that Saturday will mark the third straight week with an embarrassing incident between fan and player that causes someone to get banned for life? Probably pretty good given the way too many athletic departments have let their sidelines get out of control with celebrities, influencers, big donors, various hangers-on and lickspittles who have been incorrectly conditioned to think social media anonymity works in real life.

Add all that to a buildup of liquid courage over an intense 3 1/2-hour football game and you inevitably get some yokel who couldn't bench press a flower vase running up to a 250-pound defensive end carved out of granite, thinking they can say or do something provocative without consequence.

They should consider themselves lucky if all they get out of it is a lifetime ban rather than a trip to the hospital.

Seriously, what the heck is going on here?

First came the Alabama fan two weeks ago, who was captured on video slapping the helmet of Georgia linebacker Raylen Wilson before shoving him away with one hand while the other held a styrofoam cup.

This particular fan was sitting in the very first row, near where Georgia players were celebrating with friends and family, and Wilson initially thought it was a Georgia fan congratulating him, which is partly why he walked away without a confrontation.

But once the video began to circulate, and it became clear that this was an Alabama fan who was acting maliciously, the school identified and banned him for life from attending any other athletic events.

"It's disappointing behavior by any fan," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said.

With the amount of attention that story got, particularly around the SEC, you'd think everyone would get the message.

But in the aftermath of Florida's victory at Texas last week, a young fan wearing a burnt orange windbreaker was standing about three feet from a group of Gators when he looked right at 6-foot-6, 277-pound LJ McCray and flipped him the bird. Then, this "fan" continued to hold up his right middle finger while filming with his other hand. As a group of Florida players started to follow him, staffers stepped in to make sure the situation didn't escalate.

Maybe the craziest part of all is that this dummy was smiling through the whole thing, acting as if he's protected from anything bad that might happen to him. While we in no way condone violence or players retaliating — we've seen that before and it goes poorly for everyone — these so-called fans do not realize how little sympathy they would engender if they walked away with a few bruises.

Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte apologized in his weekly newsletter and said the matter had been addressed internally. He later told the Houston Chronicle that the offender was a local college student who attends an out-of-state university.

"Having access to our field comes with a responsibility to represent Texas with class and respect," Del Conte wrote. "This individual failed to uphold that responsibility and has been permanently banned from Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium."

The more troubling part, according to a post on X by the Houston Chronicle's Kirk Bohls, was that Del Conte "doesn't know who authorized a field pass for the young student."

While there certainly should be an audit trail linked to every field pass just for general safety and security reasons, it's not that far-fetched to come up with a scenario where a big donor who has access to a few passes gives a couple to his buddy who gives one to their snot-nosed kid who ends up acting like an idiot toward a player because their entire life has been awash in privilege and entitlement.

Thanks to social media, we see a lot of this in our world now. In so many everyday interactions, Main Character Syndrome has become the norm and shame is on the decline. Rather than engaging with the rules of a polite society, too many people want to treat their march through life as an opportunity to make content.

And that's dangerous for college sports because there has never really been much desire to erect a solid wall between player and fan.

Whether they want to admit it or not, athletic departments are in the business of selling access. For the right price, you can sit where you want, stand on the sideline, text suggestions to the coaches, maybe even get into the locker room. It's why schools have stuffed premium seats into areas that used to be empty and why they pay a lot of money for a coach to show up for an hour at a local sports bar to take questions from radio callers.

Despite the explosion of money and fame in college sports, there is still a closeness and community part of fandom that you don't get in the NFL or NBA.

Why do schools still pay coaches a lot of money to show up for an hour at some local sports bar and take questions from radio callers? Why are local businesses eager to hand out NIL deals that often require players to make in-person appearances or sign autographs? Why do schools allow field-storming after big wins when they know they'll pay a hefty fine and potentially put athletes in danger?

Allowing people to feel like they can reach out and touch the program is a feature, not a bug.

But occasionally, it does come with a downside. And if these incidents start happening on a more regular basis, it will need to be systematically addressed for the sake of the players who are expected to take the abuse of opposing fans from close range and not retaliate.

Yeah, everyone loves the images of students coming out of the stands to celebrate and tearing down goalposts after a big win. It's a part of the experience that differentiates college from the pros. But as college sports becomes more professionalized, it's fair to ask whether the field of play needs to be treated more as a workplace.

Players and coaches shouldn't have to worry that the aftermath of a game is going to turn into a melee because someone who doesn't belong on the field in the first place did something to provoke a player whose emotions were already on edge.

After the issues we've seen the last couple weeks, that's a fair concern. Expecting players to have restraint 100 percent of the time when fans lose their inhibitions seems like a bad bet. After all, it's only going to take one ugly incident to make a school look culpable for allowing that kind of access in the first place.

articles.title: Preocupación por Kompany: trasladado al hospital tras varios días con una infección vírica
articles.standfirst: El equipo alemán añadió información sobre lo ocurrido
articles.summary: Según BILD, un helicóptero medicalizado aterrizó en las instalaciones del Bayern antes de que el técnico belga fuera trasladado a un centro hospitalario de Múnich
articles.body: Vincent Kompany ha sido trasladado este viernes al hospital de Múnich, según informa BILD y el propio equipo alemán. Un helicóptero medicalizado aterrizó previamente en las instalaciones del Bayern, en la Säbener, donde se produjo la intervención. El técnico belga, de 40 años, llevaba varios días afectado por una infección vírica. Por el momento, se desconoce el motivo concreto del traslado. Los problemas de salud del entrenador se hicieron visibles el pasado sábado, durante la victoria ante el RB Leipzig por 6-1. Kompany dio la charla a sus futbolistas y tuvo que tumbarse unos minutos en el sofá de su vestuario en el Allianz Arena, tanto en el descanso como después del encuentro. Según el diario alemán, tras recuperarse brevemente al término del partido, volvió a analizar algunas jugadas en su ordenador portátil. Las entrevistas quedaron en manos de los responsables deportivos del club. BILD señala que la infección habría provocado molestias en una zona con tejido cicatricial antiguo, lo que le dificultaba acciones como subir escaleras. El lunes no dirigió el entrenamiento y, de acuerdo con el mismo medio, fue examinado de nuevo de forma exhaustiva por los médicos, con el internista del equipo, el profesor Roland Schmidt, al frente. El martes tampoco pudo ponerse al mando de la última sesión antes del compromiso europeo. Regresó al banquillo ante el Arsenal Su asistente, Aaron Danks, de 43 años, asumió la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro de la Champions League y explicó que la prioridad era que Kompany descansara y se tomara el tiempo necesario para recuperarse. El miércoles, el belga volvió a ocupar su sitio en la banda durante el empate contra el Arsenal (2-2), después de haberse perdido los entrenamientos del inicio de semana. Tras aquel partido, el propio Kompany habló de su estado de salud y reconoció que había seguido adelante pese al malestar: "Como entrenador, siempre quieres hacerlo todo y conseguirlo todo. La semana pasada contraje un virus bastante desagradable y, por supuesto, no escuché a mi cuerpo. Llegó un momento en que mi cuerpo me dijo: “¡Para ya!”".

A club statement said: , external "Terry has been receiving valuable support from the League Managers Association (LMA) in recent months, and the club will continue to stand alongside him and his family throughout his treatment and recovery.

"Everyone at AFC Wimbledon sends Terry their heartfelt best wishes as he prepares for the next stage of his treatment."

The 51-year-old joined AFC Wimbledon in May 2022 as Johnnie Jackson's assistant and helped the club win promotion to League One through the play-offs in 2025.

articles.summary: As PSG faces a scheduling conflict with their upcoming match against Lyon on the same night as the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, questions arise about whether their nominated stars will attend the prestigious event or fulfill their club duties.
articles.body: Could a sudden security postponement force Paris Saint-Germain’s brightest stars to watch their own Ballon d’Or coronation from the dugout?A last-minute police directive in Paris has triggered a bizarre logistical crisis, shifting PSG’s high-stakes Ligue 1 clash against Lyon to Monday night, placing it in a direct, agonizing bottleneck with football’s premier awards gala in London. While the club's fit nominees face a strict professional ultimatum to remain in France, a recent wave of injuries has created an ironic twist, potentially clearing the way for the squad's sidelined superstars to travel to the red carpet.Why PSG’s match with Lyon was postponedOriginally scheduled to host Lyon at the Parc des Princes on Sunday, October 25, at 8:45 p.m. local time, Paris Saint-Germain will instead play on Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m.The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) confirmed the shift on Friday, stating that it "acknowledges the order issued by the Prefecture of Police prohibiting the holding of the PSG - Lyon match, scheduled for Matchday 8 of McDonald's Ligue 1, on Sunday, October 25, at 8:45 p.m., and has decided, in agreement with Ligue 1+, to reschedule the match for Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m."This late scheduling change comes as French authorities brace for a substantial security operation over the weekend. Law enforcement resources have been heavily stretched by nationwide demonstrations following a wave of severe unrest on October 17, when rioting and looting swept through Paris and other major cities, causing widespread damage to public buildings and private businesses.Compounding the strain on police resources is Sunday’s high-profile NFL regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, hosted at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis—just ten kilometres from the Place de la Bastille, where massive weekend protests are expected to converge.As a result, France’s domestic sporting schedule has faced widespread disruptions. Local authorities previously requested that Toulouse’s fixture against Troyes be pushed from Saturday to Sunday, while both Marseille and Lille reported that their official club merchandise stores had been targeted and looted during the prior weekend's violence.The rearranged Monday night fixture carries massive sporting stakes on the pitch, bringing together two of Ligue 1’s early pacesetters. Defending champions PSG and rivals Lyon sit level at the top of the table on 14 points after seven matches, with Lyon holding the edge strictly on goal difference.The new date creates a Ballon d’Or dilemmaThe match now overlaps with the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, which is being held at the London Palladium on October 26. The gala marks the first time the award ceremony has taken place in England, with Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal among those hoping to unseat 2025 winner Ousmane Dembélé.PSG have a record 10 players on the men’s shortlist: Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Achraf Hakimi, Vitinha, Fabián Ruiz, João Neves, Willian Pacho and Ferran Torres. The club also has Warren Zaïre-Emery nominated for the Kopa Trophy, Matvey Safonov for the Yashin Trophy, Luis Enrique for Men’s Coach of the Year and PSG itself for Men’s Club of the Year.For players selected to face Lyon, the scheduling creates an obvious practical dilemma: the match in Paris clashes with the ceremony in London. Those involved are likely to prioritise their club commitments, but there has been no official confirmation of which nominees will attend the gala, whether PSG will make individual arrangements, or if the players will miss the ceremony altogether.Injured nominees may have a different choiceDembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes have been reported as injured and ruled out of the Lyon fixture. That could make attendance in London easier for them, although their travel plans have not been officially confirmed.The timing is particularly notable for Dembélé, who won the 2025 Ballon d’Or and is among the nominees again. His injury means he may be able to attend without missing the match, unlike fit teammates whose presence could be required in Paris.Last year offers a striking precedentPSG encountered a similar scheduling problem last season, when heavy rain forced their Le Classique match against Marseille to be moved to Monday, coinciding with the Ballon d’Or ceremony at which Dembélé won.Dembélé was fit and important to the team, but PSG’s management gave him special permission to miss the rescheduled fixture so he could attend the gala. His teammates played without him and lost 1-0 to Marseille, making the decision a consequential one on the pitch as well as a memorable moment in his career.This year’s circumstances differ because Dembélé is reportedly injured and unavailable for the Lyon match. He would not need the same dispensation to leave the squad for London if he is unable to play, while fit nominees could face a more difficult decision. Whether PSG grants any exceptions, and which players ultimately attend, remains unconfirmed.What happens to the nominees now?The fit PSG nominees are likely to have their club duties to consider, while the injured players may have greater flexibility. Last year’s Dembélé arrangement shows that the club can make an exception for a major awards night, but it offers no guarantee that PSG will repeat that decision for other players.For now, the clash leaves the club balancing a top-of-the-table Ligue 1 fixture against an awards ceremony featuring an unusually large share of its squad. The final attendance picture will depend on PSG’s team plans, the players’ fitness and any decisions announced by the club or ceremony organisers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carrión, ante su estreno en Butarque: “Quiero un equipo ganador y que sea reconocible”
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico pepinero debutará ante el Real Mallorca convencido de poder cambiar la dinámica del equipo
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico pepinero debutará ante el Real Mallorca convencido de poder cambiar la dinámica del equipo
articles.body: Luis Carrión afronta con ilusión y confianza su estreno en el banquillo del Leganés. El técnico debutará ante el Real Mallorca en Butarque con el reto de acabar con una preocupante racha de cuatro derrotas consecutivas, en las que los pepineros han encajado diez goles y no han conseguido marcar ninguno. Una situación que quiere revertir desde el primer día. Primeras sensaciones con la plantilla: “La primera impresión es de una plantilla con un buen nivel de trabajo, gente que quiere”. El técnico destacó también la implicación de unos futbolistas que están “dolidos con la situación y con ganas de revertirla”. El equipo que quiere construir: “Queremos un equipo reconocible, agresivo con y sin balón”. Carrión tiene clara la identidad que pretende dar al Leganés, buscando un conjunto ganador y capaz de competir ante cualquier rival. La falta de gol: “La responsabilidad del gol no tiene que recaer sólo en un jugador”. El entrenador es consciente de los problemas ofensivos del equipo, que acumula cuatro partidos sin marcar, y considera fundamental generar más ocasiones y repartir la responsabilidad entre todos sus futbolistas. El estreno ante el Mallorca: Carrión afronta su primer partido con las bajas de Morata, sancionado, y Atienza, lesionado, pero con plena confianza en su plantilla. “Me gusta el equipo y trabajaremos para que salgan los resultados”. El Ontime Butarque será el primer examen de una nueva etapa que necesita empezar a sumar cuanto antes.

articles.title: El regreso de Ronaldinho es real: jugará el 15 de noviembre en Serie C con el Rávena
articles.standfirst: Se medirá al Forli en el derbi de Romagna, ha confirmado su Presidente
articles.summary: Se medirá al Forli en el derbi de Romagna, ha confirmado su Presidente
articles.body: Lo que durante largos meses pareció simplemente una genial maniobra de marketing... ahora se convierte en real. Según ha comunicado Ignazio Cipriani, el Presidente del club de Serie C italiana (Tercera División), Ronaldinho estará en el Estadio Benelli el 15 de noviembre a las 17:30 horas para vestir la camiseta del Rávena en el derbi de Romagna contra el Forlì "La magia nunca se ha ido, ahora es el momento de traerlo de vuelta", anunció la entidad italiana. Una confirmación que amplió el Presidente de la entidad, sin dar más detalles sobre si será un retorno permanente o un partido aislado. "Nos dijeron que era imposible. El 15 de noviembre, Ronaldinho saltará al campo del Estadio Benelli vistiendo nuestra camiseta en un partido tan importante como el derbi contra el Forlì. Creímos en ello desde el primer día, y gracias a la pasión y el esfuerzo de todo nuestro equipo, hemos transformado una idea que parecía imposible en un acontecimiento que todo el mundo espera con ansias", declaró a 'ANSA' Ignazio Cipriani. El Rávena, mientras, es segundo en el Grupo B de la Serie C, a ocho puntos del liderato que ostenta ahora mismo el Spezia. Jugaría el Play-Off de ascenso a Serie B.

articles.title: Aterrizaje sin rodeos de Borja Jiménez en el Cádiz: “Tenemos que empezar con un triunfo”
articles.standfirst: El abulense, recibido por el presidente Christian Septien, llega tras dirigir ayer al Al-Ahli y se marca un objetivo inmediato ante el Ceuta
articles.summary: El abulense, recibido por el presidente Christian Septien, llega tras dirigir ayer al Al-Ahli y se marca un objetivo inmediato ante el Ceuta
articles.body: El jueves dirigía al Al-Ahli en Catar y el viernes ya estaba en la Ciudad Deportiva del Cádiz. Borja Jiménez ha cambiado de país y de banquillo sin tiempo para detenerse, con dos entrenamientos presenciales por delante antes de estrenarse el domingo ante el Ceuta. Le espera un equipo en descenso y necesitado de una reacción tras sumar siete puntos de 30 posibles bajo la dirección de Albert Celades. Todo ha sido muy rápido para Borja Jiménez. El acuerdo estaba cerrado entre el técnico y el Cádiz desde la noche del lunes, pero aún tenía cosas que hacer en Oriente Medio. Su último compromiso en la liga catarí terminó con un empate a dos ante el Al-Gharafa. Después llegó el anuncio oficial del Cádiz y una noche de viaje hasta España. Este viernes comenzó su nueva etapa en El Rosal, donde fue recibido por el presidente Christian Septien y los responsables deportivos. El mensaje del entrenador, difundido en un vídeo del club, deja poco espacio para las dudas: “Tenemos que empezar con una victoria, eso lo tengo clarísimo”. Y es que, aunque acaba de aterrizar, Borja lleva días participando en la preparación. Ha seguido entrenamientos en directo y revisado partidos y vídeos, en contacto con el 'staff' que ha conducido las sesiones tras la destitución de Albert Celades. “Sabía que teníamos que acelerar el proceso de la semana, hay muy poco tiempo”, explicó el abulense. “Muy contento de estar aquí. Quiero ayudar a revertir rápido la situación”. En un vídeo difundido por el club en sus redes sociales, Christian Septien, que llevaba semanas sin dejarse ver por Cádiz, destacó esa implicación durante la bienvenida: “Quería agradecerte que hayas venido desde Qatar y agradecerte cómo te has involucrado durante la semana. Viendo partidos, entrenamientos y vídeos. Bienvenido a tu casa”. El presidente también subrayó que el contacto había sido continuo: “Como sabes, llevamos ya una semana trabajando de forma constante contigo”. La primera sesión presencial del nuevo entrenador se ha desarrollado este viernes a las 16:30 horas, donde ya ha tenido el primer contacto físico con la plantilla. Mañana sábado será presentado a las 13:30 en el Nuevo Mirandilla y el domingo tendrá su primer examen, frente a otro equipo situado en descenso. Borja llega con experiencia en los banquillos de Mirandés, Cartagena, Deportivo, Leganés y Sporting. En Butarque consiguió un ascenso a Primera como campeón de Segunda. Ahora necesita trasladar ese conocimiento de la categoría a un Cádiz que busca estabilidad y, sobre todo, victorias. Su primer mensaje a la afición también apunta al domingo: “Tengo muchísimas ganas de veros, de conseguir los tres primeros puntos y que disfrutemos juntos”.

articles.title: Nico Raskin: Rangers midfielder 'really happy' at Scottish Premiership club but unsure about future
articles.summary: The Belgium international looked set to leave Ibrox in the summer; he is under contract until 2028; Raskin scored in Rangers' 2-2 draw at Dundee in their last Scottish Premiership match; they host St Johnstone on Saturday
articles.body:
It was widely believed that the 25-year-old midfielder, who signed from Standard Liege in January 2023, would move on after being part of the Belgium side that reached the quarter-final of the 2026 World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual winners Spain.

However, after missing a few games amid speculation about his future, Raskin has become a mainstay in Derek McInnes' side.

Asked if he had expected to leave in the summer, he replied: "Of course, when you're an ambitious player, you want to keep going higher and higher and higher, so I thought there was a point where maybe I could try to go and get a new challenge after the World Cup.

"But like I said, I've never been pushing for something because I'm really happy here, it's a big club.

"This club helped me to join the Belgian national team, which is a big thing. So I'm really calm with that.

"If something comes and everybody would be happy with it, then I would have looked to see if I could do it or not. But I don't need to push anything.

"I'm happy; the manager has been amazing with me since he arrived, so it was good this year to have that support from the manager.

"I was quite calm in the game, just taking it day by day, training after training to see where that would take me."

On the possibility of signing a new deal, he added: "I don't know, it's not up to me. It's up to the club.

"I'm just trying to work every day as hard as I can and try to give a good performance on the pitch and see what happens."

McInnes also expected Raskin to move on but is more than happy to be working with him.

Regarding the Belgian possibly agreeing a new contact, the Gers boss said: "I normally leave those sort of contract discussions between the club, the player and the agent.

"But if there was an opportunity to work with Nico beyond that, then obviously it's something that I would not be against.

"I'm enjoying working with him, but equally I understand players may well have other aspirations.

"Nico said to me that he could have had one or two things that he could have jumped at in the transfer window.

"But he's keen to be here and be part of a successful team.

"Unless something comes up that really turns his head and really turns Rangers' head, then we keep working together.

"And how long that remains, whether it's to the end of the season or whether it's beyond that, too many things can happen."

articles.title: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich manager taken to hospital after collapsing
articles.summary: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany is taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club's second team train on Friday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club's second team train on Friday.

The 40-year-old had been unwell with a virus and missed the pre-match news conference on Tuesday prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal.

The former Manchester City and Belgium defender was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday.

Reports in Germany say Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital.

"Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during an FC Bayern reserve team training session on Friday," said a statement from the Bundesliga club. , external

"The first-team head coach was watching the second string's session.

"Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical care.

"His coaching staff will oversee training and match activities until further notice."

Bayern's next game is against Freiburg in the German top flight on Sunday.

"Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure his speedy recovery," said Bayern sporting director Max Eberl.

"Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs.

"His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery."

Aaron Danks, one of Kompany's assistants, took the pre-match news conference for Bayern before the Arsenal game.

German football journalist Taufig Khalil told BBC Radio 5 Live that Kompany had been "suffering with the virus for about a week".

He added: "The thing started last weekend on Saturday against Leipzig, and that's the first time we saw Vincent Kompany [when] he didn't look very well.

"He didn't do the press conference after, and Max Eberl told us that he's suffering with a virus.

"Everybody was really surprised that Vincent Kompany was standing there with his black jacket in the pouring rain of Munich on Wednesday night against Arsenal. Everybody expected Aaron Danks to be there.

"The problem was that maybe you couldn't bench Vincent Kompany, the game was too important for him.

"Bayern Munich just told us that he's in stable conditions. There was a helicopter involved in the whole thing, which landed on the training ground at Bayern Munich, but he was not brought into the hospital by helicopter. They brought him with a medical car and he will be now there."

Kompany left his role as Burnley manager to take over at Bayern in May 2024, succeeding current England manager Thomas Tuchel.

He had won the Championship with Burnley in 2022-23 and, despite the Clarets being relegated from the Premier League under him the following season, Kompany was appointed by the Bundesliga club.

He has led Bayern to the German top-flight title in the past two seasons and reached the 2025-26 Champions League semi-finals before being beaten by eventual winners Paris St-Germain.

Kompany spent 11 years at Manchester City as a player, winning four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and four League Cups.

"Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and club legend, Vincent Kompany," said City in a post on social media. "Get well soon, Vinny."

"Everyone here at Burnley FC sends our best wishes to Vincent and we wish him a speedy recovery," said a Burnley statement.
