articles.title: Why did Spain award Lionel Messi its 'Nobel Prize'? Inside his historic win as the first individual footballer
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has made history by becoming the first individual footballer to receive Spain's prestigious Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, recognizing his unparalleled achievements in football and his philanthropic work with vulnerable children.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has added an honour unlike any of the trophies that defined his football career, receiving Spain’s prestigious Princess of Asturias Award for Sports in Oviedo on Friday. The Argentine was recognised not only for his achievements on the pitch, but also for his charitable work supporting vulnerable children. The award makes Messi the first footballer to receive the distinction individually, following earlier honours for teams and other sporting greats.Messi receives the honour in Oviedo after returning to SpainMessi was presented with the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports at the Teatro Campoamor in Oviedo on Friday, October 23, after arriving in northern Spain the previous day. The 39-year-old attended events with local schoolchildren before joining King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia and fellow award recipients for an official dinner.His visit came just weeks after he brought the curtain down on his international career with Argentina, adding a new distinction to a career already marked by record-breaking trophies and individual awards. The Inter Miami forward is expected to return to the United States ahead of his club’s October 24 fixture against the New York Red Bulls.The Princess of Asturias Awards are presented annually by the Princess of Asturias Foundation across eight categories, recognising achievements in fields including sport, the arts, literature, science and public affairs. First established in 1981 as the Prince of Asturias Awards, the prizes are often described as Spain’s equivalent of the Nobel honours.The sports award is presented each October in Oviedo and includes a Joan Miró sculpture, a diploma, an insignia and €50,000. The ceremony takes place at the Teatro Campoamor, a historic opera house that has become the awards’ home.Why Messi was selected, beyond his extraordinary trophy collectionThe jury announced Messi as the 2026 recipient on June 3, choosing him from 27 candidates representing 12 nationalities. Its decision recognised his exceptional talent and career, while also pointing to his consistency, humility, team-first approach and conduct on the pitch.Messi’s record provides a substantial sporting case. He has won 47 team trophies, including the 2022 FIFA World Cup with Argentina, four Champions League titles and 10 La Liga championships with Barcelona. He also holds the record for Ballon d’Or wins, with eight, and has claimed six European Golden Shoes, while scoring 936 official senior career goals.His career has continued beyond Barcelona, where he spent the bulk of his club years, through two seasons at Paris Saint-Germain and his move to Inter Miami after Argentina’s World Cup triumph. The Princess of Asturias Award, however, recognises more than the accumulation of titles and records.The foundation also highlighted Messi’s charitable work, particularly his support for children facing vulnerable circumstances. He has served as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador since 2010 and runs the Leo Messi Foundation, which supports initiatives focused on children’s health, education and access to opportunities.After learning he had been selected, Messi acknowledged the importance Spain has held in his life, saying: “This award has a very special value for me.”A first for an individual footballer, with a strong Spanish connectionAlthough footballers have received the Princess of Asturias Award before, Messi is the first to win it individually. Spain’s men’s national team received the honour in 2010 after winning the World Cup, while Iker Casillas and Xavi Hernández shared it in 2012.Messi’s connection with Spain runs through much of his personal and professional life. He moved from Argentina at 13 to join Barcelona’s La Masia academy and acquired Spanish citizenship in September 2005. His formative years and the peak of his club career unfolded in the country, even as he remained Argentina’s defining football figure.The award is restricted to Spanish nationals, making Messi’s citizenship relevant to his eligibility. His selection also reflects the scale of his impact in Spain, where Barcelona helped shape the career that would eventually make him one of football’s most celebrated players.Messi joins a distinguished list of sporting recipientsThe Argentine joins a roster of previous sports award winners that includes Serena Williams, honoured in 2025, badminton player Carolina Marín in 2024 and marathon runner Eliud Kipchoge in 2023. Rafael Nadal, Michael Schumacher, Fernando Alonso, Pau and Marc Gasol, and Spain’s 2010 World Cup-winning team have also received the distinction.The award’s emphasis on sporting achievement and social contribution helps explain why Messi’s selection reaches beyond his familiar records. His football career has brought him global recognition, while his foundation and UNICEF work have helped direct some of that influence towards children’s health and education.For Messi, the honour arrives after an international career that ended with Argentina’s greatest prize and while he continues playing for Inter Miami. It recognises the footballer’s achievements, but also the values and charitable work the jury believes have accompanied them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo y otro 'gol fantasma' en la carrera hacia los 1.000
articles.standfirst: OPTA le da el tanto a Girotto en propia puerta; la liga saudí y Al Nassr, a Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.summary: OPTA le da el tanto a Girotto en propia puerta; la liga saudí y Al Nassr, a Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.body: 16 años después de aquel 'compartido' gol entre Cristiano Ronaldo y Pepe en Anoeta, un 'gol fantasma' vuelve a cruzarse en la carrera de CR7 hacia los 1.000 tantos oficiales. El luso, según OPTA, se queda sin su 0-2 ante Al Faysaly (victoria 1-3 de Al Nassr) en el partido disputado este viernes en la liga de Arabia Saudí. Tanto la liga saudí como Al Nassr dan el gol a Cristiano, su número 982, pero OPTA, el proveedor de estadísticas que suministra a prácticamente la totalidad de las webs y aplicaciones de resultados, va por otro camino: gol en propia puerta del brasileño Andrei Girotto. La acción de la polémica es la del 0-2 de Al Nassr: un centro perfecto de Joao Félix que, a priori, Cristiano cabeceaba de forma impecable para hacer el segundo. Las imágenes, sin embargo, dejan abierto el debate: ¿la toca él o es el jugador de Al Faysaly el que desvía?.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian, Texas Using New AI Platform 'Bevo Lab' to Assist with Decision Making
articles.summary: University of Texas head football coach Steve Sarkisian now has access to new artificial intelligence software and insights thanks to an innovative Longhorns initiative.
articles.body:
University of Texas head football coach Steve Sarkisian now has access to new artificial intelligence software and insights thanks to an innovative Longhorns initiative.

Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte divulged that information in an interview with Karoline Leonard of the Austin American-Statesman this week, noting that Texas' Bevo Lab AI platform is "the new wave."

Conte also clarified previous comments he made that suggested Texas used the Bevo Lab insights during last week's 27-24 loss to Florida:

According to Leonard, Bevo Lab will be available to coaches, trainers, nutritionists, student-athletes and analysts for every Longhorns sports team.

The platform is sponsored by Dell, Google and SHI International, and it will use Google's Cloud Platform and Gemini agentic AI system.

Del Conte called the development "earth-shattering," while UT Business Sports Institute founder Kirk Goldsberry added, "We're trying to put good data and good intelligence in front of our coaches, so that they can make informed decisions and informed strategies to help us ultimately win more competitions at The University of Texas."

Although Bevo Lab made its debut last week with the football team, every varsity sport at the University of Texas will soon have access to the platform.

Following a 4-0 start, which included wins over ranked opponents in Ohio State and Tennessee, Texas is now 4-2 on the heels of back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida.

Now, the Longhorns are perhaps entering a must-win scenario on Saturday against No. 7 Ole Miss.

Should No. 19 Texas lose, it could virtually mark the end of the Longhorns' pursuit of a College Football Playoff berth.

The 40-year-old was observing the session when the incident occurred, the German club said.“Kompany will undergo comprehensive examinations at the hospital and remain under medical care,” the team stated. “In the meantime, his coaching staff will manage training and match-related activities.”Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club would give Kompany all the time he needed to recover, stressing that his health remained the priority.“Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority,” Eberl said. “We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure that he recovers quickly. Vinnie will receive all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs.”Kompany had previously been diagnosed with a viral infection, which forced him to miss a training session and a press conference on Tuesday. However, he returned to the dugout for Bayern's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday.After the match, Kompany admitted that he had tried to carry on despite being unwell and had ignored the signals his body was giving him.The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 at home against Arsenal in the Champions League earlier this week, are due to travel to Freiburg on Sunday.Bayern are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday. articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga considera que la operación refuerza la nueva etapa del club y confirma el atractivo del fútbol español para la inversión internacional
articles.body: El presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas, mostró este viernes su respaldo a la operación anunciada por el Valencia para dar entrada Pitchwise en su accionariado, con la adquisición del 42% del capital social, y puso el foco en el papel desempeñado por Kiat Lim al frente de la entidad. "La entrada de nuevos socios supone un paso decisivo en el relevo liderado por Kiat Lim, que continuará como presidente mientras Meriton mantiene la participación mayoritaria", afirmó Tebas en unas declaraciones difundidas tras el anuncio de la operación. El dirigente de la patronal destacó además el trabajo realizado por el máximo responsable valencianista desde su llegada a la presidencia. "Desde que asumió la presidencia en 2025, ha conseguido asegurar la financiación del Nou Mestalla y ahora incorpora socios de máximo prestigio internacional", señaló. Tebas calificó el acuerdo como "una noticia muy positiva para el Valencia y también para toda la ciudad de Valencia" y destacó que la alianza "no solo aporta capital, sino que incorpora socios con una enorme experiencia en gestión deportiva e inversores de primer nivel mundial". Sobre las dimensiones de la operación, recordó que "valora al club en 1.250 millones de euros y supone la entrada con un 42% del capital". A su juicio, este movimiento "refleja la fortaleza y el potencial de todos los activos del Valencia, desde sus equipos masculino y femenino hasta el nuevo estadio". El presidente de LaLiga también enmarcó la operación en el creciente interés de la inversión internacional por el fútbol español. "Es importante destacar que inversores de este nivel no solo confíen en el Valencia, sino que decidan invertir en clubes de LaLiga", manifestó. Por último, sostuvo que la llegada de estos nuevos socios "acredita el gran trabajo realizado en el Valencia en los últimos años" y "vuelve a poner en valor a LaLiga como una competición atractiva y sostenible económicamente para la gran inversión internacional a largo plazo".

articles.title: Messi recibe el Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes y se gana una gran ovación

articles.summary: La Princesa Leonor fue la encargada de entregárselo en presencia de los Reyes
articles.body: Lionel Messi (Rosario, 1987) fue galardonado esta tarde con el Premio Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes en una ceremonia solemne en el Teatro Campoamor de Oviedo, habitual sede de estos Premios que reúnen cada año a lo más destacado de las Artes, las Ciencias, la Cultura y el Deporte. Leo recibió el galardón de manos de la Princesa Leonor, en presencia del Rey Felipe VI y la Reina Leticia. El Teatro Campomar brindó a Leo una tremenda ovación... que llegó hasta la Argentina, patria del crack. Messi llegó en el coche oficial al Teatro a eso de las 18.10 (20 minutos antes del acto) y avanzó hacia el recinto ante cientos de personas que se agolpaban a verle a él, especialmente en algunos casos, y al resto de premiados. Leo es cuatro veces campeón de la Champions, campeón del Mundo, bicampeón de América y jugador con casi todos los records de este deporte a nivel mundial. Pero eso no es suficiente para ser Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes. El Jurado -el director de MARCA, Juan Ignacio Gallardo, es uno de sus integrantes- ha apreciado también la labor solidaria del argentino: su trabajo, por ejemplo, con la Fundación Leo Messi y como embajador de UNICEF, enfocado en promover el acceso a la educación y el cuidado de la salud para niños en situación de vulnerabilidad. Hace poco (otro ejemplo) donó un dinero para ayudar a restaurar la Sierra madrileña quemada por los incendios del pasado verano. Eso... más todo lo que hace y no se sabe públicamente. Un aspecto esencial para este Premio Princesa de Asturias. Tras la ceremonia, Leo saldrá directamente hacia el aeropuerto de Asturias para volar directamente hasta Nueva York, donde mañana juega con el Inter Miami por la MLS.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta admits 'not good signs' as Arsenal suffer HUGE Bukayo Saka injury blow
articles.summary: Arsenal will be without star winger Bukayo Saka for their upcoming Premier League fixture against Everton after he sustained a thigh injury. Manager Mikel Ar...
articles.body:
Arsenal will be without star winger Bukayo Saka for their upcoming Premier League fixture against Everton after he sustained a thigh injury. Manager Mikel Arteta admitted the early signs are concerning, with the player set for an MRI scan to determine the full extent of the issue.

Saka has been officially ruled out of Saturday's Premier League fixture against Everton. The 25-year-old is dealing with a thigh injury and requires further medical assessment before a return timeline can be established.

The England international sustained the issue just ten minutes into 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich . He attempted to continue but was ultimately forced off the pitch due to the problem.

Arteta admits concerning signs for winger

The precise severity of the injury remains unclear, prompting significant concern for Arsenal. Arteta confirmed that the player is undergoing further evaluation to understand the true extent of the damage.

"He's going for an MRI this afternoon because he had a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the severity of the injury. We will know tomorrow," Arteta told a press conference on Friday.

"We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. When a player is struggling to walk off the pitch and he's restricted in his movement, they are not good signs. So again, let's be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment and then let you know."

Arsenal boss frustrated by fixture congestion

The timing of the setback has amplified concerns over player welfare at the highest level. Following the injury to his star winger, Arteta took the opportunity to highlight the immense physical strain placed on modern squads.

The Arsenal manager actively called for greater consideration from football's governing bodies. He stressed that teams are being pushed to their absolute physical limits.

"If they can support the amount we are putting into these players, it would be really appreciated," he said. "We have to play three times in less than six days, the games are so demanding, we are chasing until the last minute."

Arsenal must now navigate their immediate domestic duties without one of their most influential attackers. The club will eagerly await the weekend MRI results to establish whether the winger faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

The immediate focus shifts to securing three points at home against Everton this Saturday. Arteta will need to shuffle his attacking options to compensate for the significant absence on the right flank.

The relentless run of fixtures will not ease up after the league clash. Arsenal are subsequently scheduled to visit fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup fourth round on Tuesday.

articles.title: Celtic Target January Defensive Midfielder: Has The Summer Planning Failed?
articles.summary: Celtic’s domestic form has offered encouragement, but their European campaign has exposed questions about the balance of Martin O’Neill’s squad. The Scottish...
articles.body:
Celtic's domestic form has offered encouragement, but their European campaign has exposed questions about the balance of Martin O'Neill's squad. The Scottish champions have lost their first three Europa League league-phase fixtures, leaving little room for further mistakes.

A 7-1 victory over Hearts displayed Celtic's attacking threat, yet domestic results cannot disguise the demands of European football. O'Neill needs dependable options across the pitch, particularly when injuries and suspensions disrupt his preferred starting XI.

Summer recruitment brought significant changes to the squad. Celtic signed striker Kasper Høgh for a reported £11 million and added winger Haissem Hassan, while several late arrivals expanded their options. However, the departures of Arne Engels, Daizen Maeda and Reo Hatate reduced the squad's established quality in key areas.

Those sales reportedly generated a net transfer surplus of £35.5 million, although Celtic must balance that figure against their recruitment costs and other financial commitments. The late arrivals offered additional depth, but integrating new players takes time, particularly when the manager needs immediate consistency in European competition.

Callum McGregor remains central to Celtic's midfield structure. The captain provides positional discipline and helps the team move possession forward, yet relying heavily on one player creates obvious risks across a demanding season. Mika Baur, Joël van den Berg and Oliver Sørensen provide midfield alternatives, although the squad still needs a specialist defensive presence.

According to Celts Are Here , Celtic continue to prioritise a defensive midfielder for January while assessing centre-backs to address defensive absences. Recruitment chief Tam Mullen faces the task of finding players who can contribute immediately rather than requiring months of adaptation.

Does Celtic's January recruitment expose a failure in summer planning?

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – OCTOBER 18: Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic, gestures before the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Celtic's reported priorities look like a tactical necessity, but they also raise questions about the club's summer recruitment strategy. A specialist defensive midfielder would protect the centre-backs, close passing lanes and give McGregor greater freedom to control possession without carrying the entire defensive workload.

The club should seek a physically strong, tactically disciplined midfielder who can win duels and distribute the ball cleanly under pressure. Central defence needs similar attention, although Celtic must assess their returning players before committing substantial fees to another signing.

The £35.5 million surplus makes the lack of balance harder to defend. January recruitment must address specific weaknesses rather than chase names or repeat the late-window scramble. Celtic need fewer emergency solutions and more reliable players capable of handling the pressure at Celtic Park.

According to journalist Florian Plettenberg , Dani Olmo has no intention of leaving Barcelona, with sources close to the midfielder confirming that he is happy at the Catalan club despite reported interest from Bayern Munich .

A January departure is currently ruled out, while the Bundesliga champions are also not actively working on a deal for the Spain international.

Dani Olmo happy at Barcelona despite Bayern Munich interest

Despite speculation linking him with a return to the Bundesliga, Olmo remains committed to his future at Barcelona.

People close to the player have confirmed that he is happy with his situation at the club and is not considering an exit at this stage.

Bayern Munich have been linked with the midfielder amid reports that the German side were monitoring potential attacking reinforcements.

Not going anywhere. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Olmo has been admired by the Bavarian giants ever since his time with RB Leipzig. His technical quality and versatility make him an attractive profile, but reported interest has not translated into concrete transfer activity.

The latest information suggests there is currently no deal being pursued by Bayern. There are no active negotiations over a move, and a transfer during the January window is not on the agenda.

Olmo's long-term contract provides further stability amid the transfer rumours. The Spain international is tied to Barcelona until 2030, leaving the club in a strong position and removing any immediate contractual pressure to consider a sale.

Since returning to Barcelona in 2024, Olmo has been part of Hansi Flick's plans, offering creativity and flexibility in attacking areas.

Under contract until 2030. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

He can operate centrally as an attacking midfielder or provide options in wider positions or even as a false nine, making him a useful asset for the team.

For now, neither a potential January departure nor a move to Bayern Munich appears to be on the cards.

Olmo's stated happiness at Barcelona, combined with his long-term contract, points towards continuity rather than an imminent change of club.

Having suffered an injury during the recent game against PSG , in what his 100th game for the club, the 28-year-old Spaniard will be focused on recovering at the earliest possible.

articles.title: Arch Manning's CFB Transfer Portal Landing Spot Predicted by Insider Amid Texas Benching Buzz
articles.summary: One person connected to Texas quarterback Arch Manning reportedly feels he is more likely to transfer to another school than enter the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
One person connected to Texas quarterback Arch Manning reportedly feels he is more likely to transfer to another school than enter the 2027 NFL draft.

NFL Network's Tom Pelissero said around the 36:45 mark of Friday's Bill Simmons Podcast he had texted someone who knew Manning to ask where the quarterback was likely to end up next season.

"His response was, 'Ole Miss,'" Pelissero said.

Both Manning's grandfather Archie Manning and his uncle Eli Manning starred for, and later had their numbers retired by, Ole Miss.

Manning said during his own recruitment process his top choices had been Texas, Georgia and Alabama.

The Rebels could be looking for a quarterback next offseason. Trinidad Chambliss is both in his final year of collegiate eligibility and listed as the No. 14 overall prospect on Bleacher Report's latest NFL draft big board .

The speculation comes after Texas coach Steve Sarkisian told reporters he is hoping to see "a better version of Arch" after consecutive Longhorns losses to unranked opponents.

Steve Sarkisian also said Manning's QB1 status would be re-evaluated after No. 19 Texas matchups up Saturday against No. 7 Ole Miss.

Eli Manning, who spent four seasons with the Rebels between 2000 and 2003, talked about the positives of a longer college career when asked about his nephew's future in an appearance earlier this month on the Colin Cowherd Podcast .

"I think that's the whole point of college, is to enjoy being in college, to get better every year," Eli said. "To play more games, to get better, to get more prepared for the NFL, to try to win a national championship or an SEC championship... I'm proud of Arch, and how he's handled this, and his mindset. He's focused on the next game, this year, and just doing his job."

Manning, initially projected as a candidate for the 2027 draft, has struggled to develop consistently in his second season as a full-time starter for the Longhorns.

Whether Manning is able to hold off backup quarterback KJ Lacey from getting a shot at the starter's job this weekend could determine what his future with the Longhorns looks like going forward.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso: Chelsea manager sits down with former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher for new 'Boss' YouTube series
articles.summary: Watch Chelsea vs Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday Night Football from 5pm on Sky Sports Premier League; kick-off 5.30pm; watch Jamie Carragher's full interview with Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports Premier League at 7.30pm on Sunday October 25
articles.body:
"It was about the timing. For me, it was the right timing after Leverkusen. After Madrid, I had my time off and I wanted to have that good feeling, that good connection about where to go.

"I had no link to Chelsea, but with the potential that was here, a few things could change and I thought we could start the journey together.

"I had a feeling that the very strong base of the squad was very good and with some updates, some improvements, some new signings, we could have a solid team. And that it was going to be a project.

"It's not that, in year one it's already done; we know it might take some more years, but the first year is important. It's just starting but, so far, the feeling that we could be aligned taking decisions is going to be important."

Did you think about the Chelsea ownership coming into initial talks?

"From outside, I had the view of what I read, what I saw about the team, but then you get to know the people, you get to know their analysis, the things they have done, the things they thought could be done better, where we were and where we wanted to take the club.

"Knowing that, in many processes, many decisions, I was going to be part of it, was important. There is the ownership, the sporting director and me, but we are always connected and we have good communication.

"That's basic, to take responsibility. Things after can go well or not go well because this is football, but in the end, you want to feel part of it."

Was Chelsea's managerial history something you thought about?

"No, it was not a worry because I know what you need to get results, but I had the feeling we were on the same page.

"We knew that where we want to be next year or in two years will take time and this is the process of building things the right way and that's why the first phase we have improved in the team has been good.

"It's just seven games, but we have a clear direction of what we want. Zero worry about this. This is football, you need to get the results. But to have the feeling we are doing things in the right way and that we have a plan is as important for me as the results."

Is winning the Premier League, getting back into the Champions League in the plan?

"In the medium to long-term, yes. We know that takes time and many right decisions. We won't make all the right decisions but, for me, being involved in the key decisions is as important as the rest.

"This is the ambition of the club. This club has won Champions Leagues and Premier Leagues not so long ago and we want to be back there, but we are not stupid to think this has to come right now. Time will tell when that can come."

Is the set-up different to your previous experiences?

"My experience in Germany is different from my experience in Spain and now. In Germany, you work very closely with the sporting director every day. That's very different from England.

"I had that relationship with Simon Rolfs where he was in the office with me every day, but not to say 'You need to do this!'

"It was to chat about the momentum of one player or a player is in a bad mood or we have had talks. Normal things. In the end, this close relationship made us a very good tandem, and it worked really well.

"At Chelsea, Sam (Jewell), Paul (Winstanley), Joe (Shields) are really close to the team as well."

What are your early memories of joining Liverpool?

"I remember not many English players used to watch LaLiga, but you were one of the ones watching LaLiga, Barcelona and Real Madrid, of course, but Atletico, Deportivo La Coruna.

"We used those games to talk more about football. We started getting to know each other and you were football mad, I was football mad.

"I learned as well that you need to earn the respect of the guys that were there. You need to have a proper impact on Stevie [Gerrard] Carra, Didi Hamann, Sami Hyypia. I knew I needed to earn my place, I need to earn my respect.

"Happily, it didn't take too long. It didn't take as long as it could coming from Real Sociedad, being 21. It was quite quick.

"I remember Bolton was proper, with Sam Allardyce. Gary Speed tackled me and said 'Welcome to the Premier League!'

"One of the first games was against Norwich at home and we won 3-0 and I played a very good game. Then people start respecting you and saying 'He can play' and, little by little, you start making your own things in the club and you get the respect of the established and local players.

"That was very important because, if not, you can struggle with the adaptation at the beginning."

What are the biggest differences between when you came to the Premier League as a player to what you see now as a manager?

"I would say the gap between the top clubs and the rest, 20 years ago, was much bigger than it is. The players are more complete. You hardly see a player that is not so fit or not so prepared physically.

"Tactically, the gameplans are really sophisticated nowadays. I'm still getting into the tempo of the Premier League because, for me, it has been a change. I try to learn as quickly as possible, but now it's very sophisticated, even the squads are so complete.

"Something has not changed: the energy that is created in the stadiums. For me, it feels the same. At the noise... we were playing against Everton and the noise and energy that was created in this stadium, that has not changed.

"For me, it's very different to the sounds of the Bundesliga or Spain. My first game against Fulham we played in the Premier League, I said 'This smells like the Premier League!'"

What do you mean about still getting up to speed?

"Before, you knew the top teams could play. But you knew, with the other teams, if you were going to press a little bit, even with one less player, normally they would play long and you would have to be ready.

"Now, that's not enough. Now, you need to prepare what's going to be the trigger point from one side; find solutions to that, so all the teams are much more complete.

"The game is much more sophisticated in the way that it has developed a lot. Teams have solutions and very good patterns."

Is there a certain methodology behind Spain's football success?

"Yes, there is a big methodology, but it has been built for 20 years. It is not something that has been built in two years.

"For example, Luis de la Fuente has been part of the youth national teams for a lot of time and he knows them very well. These players have played together for a long time and when they were 17,18, they were already playing together and they became elite players playing together.

"Now, they have this connection. You see that they are so dominant in how they play and this has a lot to do with the work the clubs do.

"I am from Real Sociedad and the way they work there, they put a lot of focus on the young players and they give them the potential. But I have to be honest, here at Chelsea they work really well and I'm really impressed with some of the young players we have.

"As well, I see the English team - they are getting there. With Thomas Tuchel, they nearly got to the final, they got to the semis. This England team is getting close. You see the players and they are very good players. They need to take the next step to develop to be winning something. They are not too far."

Why do England not produce the types of players that can control big games?

"To reach such control in the Premier League is very difficult. I think you have to be a top, top team and top players if you are able to control the game in such a manner to be so dominant.

"We are not the quickest, but we need to think quick and the players they need to think quick. That's why they develop game intelligence, awareness.

"Rodri, for example, is one step ahead, one metre ahead. How? Training, habits. The same way Sergio Busquets used to do that. He was not the quickest, but he was the smartest on the pitch and that's a pattern that is repeated in Spain because of the collective purpose of the development of the team."

What are the differences between the top managers you worked under and what did you take from them?

"Each one was really important at that stage of my career. For example, being 21/22 at Liverpool, if I had Carlo Ancelotti, it's different to when I had Ancelotti when I was 30 at Real Madrid.

"At that time, I needed a lot of tactical input, I needed a lot of explanation and Rafa Benitez was very good at that. After, I became more mature as a player.

"I then went to Madrid and I was mainly with Jose Mourinho and with Ancelotti, but that's about competing, about your mentality. I was a good player, but I could get better. It was about competing, about a winning mentality, about being tougher and I got more mature in Madrid.

"My last spell in Munich was like, after the university degree you want to have a Masters. I worked with Pep. I was so curious about why they played so well and I wanted to be inside.

"That last stage of my career in Munich made my transition to try to become a coach. I started thinking about the processes, how things happen, how you need to work and I paid a lot of attention in those years because I knew the end was getting closer and, at the end, I was going to try eventually to try to become a coach."

Did you ever speak to those managers about becoming a coach?

"With Ancelotti and with Pep. I remember my last year with Ancelotti, he invited me to do a team talk in pre-season. Pep had many midfield players where he had a good connection. For me, that was no surprise that I was so interested in the end to try to eventually become a coach."

When did you start having your own ideas?

"For me, it was more about how did I feel with a group? How did I feel talking to a group? The connection I had with the players, how I managed telling people they weren't going to play. If those decisions stress you so much, you know the job is so hard and can be so demanding.

"If you understand them as part of the job and you enjoy them somehow, that's when you can take the job naturally. I felt it. After, let's talk about football.

"I was a midfielder, so I was about control: how to control the game, how to give it more balance, how to have distances, how to not be up and down. That was how I started, but after it's about adapting to the players you have, the league where you are.

"For example, I went to Leverkusen and the team was in a difficult position. We became a very counter-attacking team. I saw the team and said 'Now we are in a difficult position and it's not about trying to play the nicest game, it's about competing'.

"We changed the system, we were very compact, defending tight and very good on the counter-attack and we ended up playing the semi-finals of the Europa League and qualifying. I have ideas and what I like, but you try to adapt as well."

articles.title: Aston Villa vs Manchester City: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: Man City are the only team with a perfect Premier League record, but face a Villa side determined to climb the table.
articles.body:
Who: Aston Villa vs Manchester City What: English Premier League Where: Villa Park in Birmingham, United Kingdom When: Saturday, October 22 at 12:30pm (11:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera will bring you all the build-up, before our live text commentary stream from 9:30am (08:30 GMT).

Manchester City can continue to put their off-field woes to one side in Saturday’s early kickoff in the Premier League when they travel to Aston Villa, where they will move six points clear at the top with a win.

Holders Arsenal entertain Everton later in the day and will very much hope to extend their winning run in the league to a third match.

City do, however, have a 100 percent record from their first seven games in the league this season, a run that defies the guilty verdict by an independent commission regarding more than 100 breaches of the competition’s financial rules.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at City’s trip to Villa Park, where the Cityzens ’ siege mentality is expected to continue.

Foden can be one of Premier League’s best again, says Maresca

Enzo Maresca said it is his job as Manchester City boss to help Phil Foden rediscover his best form after the England international ended his long goal drought.

Foden had not scored for 10 months before netting in City’s 3-2 win over Ipswich last weekend and then scored a Champions League hat-trick in a 5-1 rout of AEK Athens on Tuesday.

The 26-year-old swept the board of personal awards for the Premier League’s best player in the 2023/24 season after a 27-goal campaign.

But Foden, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, has failed to hit top form for the past two seasons.

“Since we started, I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning. Just to show him, I don’t know if love is the right word to use, but just to show him how important he is,” said Maresca, who took charge of City in June.

“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago, so I know how, for different reasons, the last few years it was not good enough.

“When you have more players like Phil available, you are a better team because again it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players, you improve the team.

“So for me, I think it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England.”

How have Maresca and Man City shaped up this season?

Other than a 4-2 Champions League defeat by holders Paris Saint-Germain, Maresca has made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium.

The Italian is the first manager ever to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club.

However, City’s fine form has been overshadowed by the threat of severe sanctions against the club for the widespread flouting of Premier League financial rules.

A large points deduction, which could lead to relegation, is likely unless City win their appeal.

Maresca said the mood in the dressing room remained buoyant despite the cloud hanging over the club.

“In any club, when you lose important players, many important players, and you lose the manager after 10 years, it always takes time to compete again,” he said on Thursday.

“But this organisation last summer changed many important players, changed the manager after 10 years, and we are competing at the moment.”

Villa sit 12th in the table, but a win would propel them to sixth, at least for a couple of hours. Under former Arsenal manager Unai Emery, Villa have been regulars among the European spots in recent seasons, and were even challengers for the title at one point.

This term has provided a sterner examination of their credentials after the exit of a number of the top stars of recent campaigns, including Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez to Chelsea, Youri Tielemans to City’s rivals United and Ollie Watkins to Al-Hilal.

The Midlands club, who beat Freiburg 3-0 to win last season’s UEFA Europa League, are on a six-match unbeaten run – of which they have won five – across the league and Champions League.

What happened the last time Aston Villa played Manchester City?

Villa were 2-1 winners at City in Pep Guardiola’s last game in charge on the final day of last season.

Antoine Semenyo gave City the lead, but an Ollie Watkins brace turned the game.

What happened in Aston Villa and Man City’s corresponding fixture last season?

Villa emerged with a 1-0 win in their Premier League clash at Villa Park last October. Matty Cash scored the only goal.

When did Man City last beat Aston Villa?

City last beat Villa when they were 2-1 winners in the Premier League fixture between the sides at Etihad Stadium in April 2025.

Marcus Rashford, on loan from United, levelled matters from the penalty spot after Bernardo Silva’s opener, but Matheus Nunes sealed the win for the home side.

When did Man City last win at Aston Villa?

City have not won at Villa Park since December 2021, when Ruben Diaz and Silva netted in the first half of the Premier League match. Watkins’s strike in the second period proved only a consolation.

The Opta supercomputer has given City a 43 percent chance of winning the match, while offering Villa a 32 percent chance of victory.

This is the 186th meeting between the sides, with City winning 82 times and Villa emerging victorious on 61 occasions. There have been 42 draws in the fixture that dates back to 1899 – and a 2-1 home win for Villa.

Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka miss out through injury. Johan Manzambi and Modou Keba Cisse both face fitness tests.

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson

Forward Antoine Semenyo is set for a lengthy spell out ⁠with a knee injury, while wing back Nico O’Reilly and midfielders Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes are doubts.

League-leading scorer Erling Haaland was rested for Tuesday’s 5-1 Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens because of a knock but is expected to be available against Villa.

articles.title: El Granada se cobra una nueva víctima a cabezazo limpio y prosigue con su escalada
articles.standfirst: Rodelas y Jorge Pascual firman su cuarta victoria seguida ante un Valladolid que sigue sin ganar a domicilio pese al golazo de Garriel
articles.summary: Rodelas y Jorge Pascual firman su cuarta victoria seguida ante un Valladolid que sigue sin ganar a domicilio pese al golazo de Garriel
articles.body: El Granada completó un nuevo ejercicio de mucho oficio. Dos cabezazos de Rodelas y Jorge Pascual le valieron para doblegar al Valladolid en Los Cármenes y confirmar su gran momento de forma, pues firma así su cuarta victoria consecutiva y asalta los puestos de 'playoffs' provisionalmente. Los rojiblancos supieron aprovechar sus oportunidades para ponerse por delante y reponerse con carácter cuando el Valladolid consiguió el empate. Y es que los de Escribá lo intentaron sin descanso, pero más allá del golazo de Garriel, apenas pudieron hacer mella en la muralla nazarí y continúan así sin ganar a domicilio tras seis desplazamientos. El pitido inicial actuó como espoleta y el partido entró pronto en ebullición, sin tiempo de presentaciones, con ambos conjuntos buscando hacer daño al rival desde los primeros compases del duelo, sin concesiones y con un ritmo endiablado. Las primeras llegadas con peligro corrieron a cargo del Valladolid, pero Ponceau disparó demasiado alto, Barberá no resolvió bien ante Alberto Flores y el meta local le hizo un auténtico paradón a bocajarro a Tay Abed. Así las cosas, el Granada respondió de la forma más efectiva y contundente posible, abriendo el marcador en un centro teledirigido de José Arnaiz desde la izquierda que Rodelas, con un cabezazo de nueve, se encargó en transformar. Incluso pudo llegar el segundo a renglón seguido, pero Aceves lo evitó con una gran parada plena de reflejos ante otro cabezazo de Jorge Pascual a centro de Diallo. Los de Escribá no descompusieron tras el golpe recibido y se hicieron con la iniciativa en el juego, probando suerte Thiago Ojeda, mientras los andaluces dieron un paso atrás, esperando agrupados para explotar la velocidad de sus atacantes, generando peligro cada vez que superaban los tres cuartos del campo, aunque Jorge Pascual y José Arnaiz no acertaron. Aunque lo intentaban, los pucelanos no encontraban argumentos suficientes como para romper la resistencia de los rojiblancos que, como en los partidos anteriores, no mostraban apenas fisuras en su entramado defensivo. En la reanudación el Valladolid salió a por todas y Barberá volvió a tener una buena ocasión que taponó Manu Lama, mientras que Alberto Flores volvió a resultar providencial ante Arnu primero y el propio Barberá después. Lo que ya no pudo evitar es que el derechazo de Garriel se colara por toda la escuadra tras un robo de Juric. El Granada, lejos de arrugarse, mostró carácter y Pacheta realizó un triple cambio para variar el rumbo que tomaba el partido y el efecto fue inmediato, pues Jorge Pascual puso el 2-1 al cabecear un gran servicio de Gumbau también desde la banda izquierda. Respondió Fran Escribá con otro triple cambio y de hecho Van Duiven, uno de los recién ingresados, rondó el empate en una salida en falso del meta local. En la recta final Aceves evitó el 3-1 en una falta cerrada de Alcaraz que se disponía a cabecear Jorge Pascual y el partido se fue diluyendo entre los intentos blanquivioletas por buscar la igualada, sobre todo en sendos cabezazos del joven Tomy Fernández que uno salió rozando el poste y el segundo lo atajó Alberto Flores. Incluso hubo tiempo para que David Torres viera la roja directa, tras la intervención del VAR, por derribar a Emeka cuando entraba solo en el área.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders are unionizing
articles.summary: America’s highest-profile cheerleading squad has won a victory of its own: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have formed a union.
articles.body: America’s highest-profile cheerleading squad has won a victory of its own: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have formed a union. The union is believed to be the first in the nation among all pro-sports cheerleading squads, outside of a short-lived effort by the Buffalo Bills’ “Buffalo Jills” in the mid-1990s. The Dallas cheerleaders’ bargaining unit has already been recognized by the Dallas Cowboys, according to a brief joint press release issued Friday by the team and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association. The agreement came after “meaningful discussion” between the two sides, the release said. The next step will be bargaining for an official contract for the cheerleaders. The squad currently consists of 36 active members, though it is not clear how many will be officially represented by the union. “The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for their talent and dedication they exhibit,” the two groups said in the release. Representatives for the Cheerleaders Association, which represents the squad, and the Dallas Cowboys did not immediately respond to requests for additional comment. The announcement comes in the wake of a multiseason Netflix series, “America’s Sweethearts,” that has documented the ups and downs of the cheerleaders’ on- and offseason lives. The attention brought by the series helped earn them a 400% raise for the 2025 season, with some veteran dancers slated to receive more than $75 an hour, according to a New York Times report. An earlier lawsuit by a former cheerleader had accused the Cowboys of paying her less than minimum wage. The team ended up settling the suit. During the Cowboys’ 1990s heyday, the cheerleaders made as little as $15 per game, according to The Dallas Morning News. The squad dates to 1961 but didn’t professionalize until the early 1970s, when Cowboys President Tex Schramm hired local choreographer Texie Waterman, who helped come up with the squad’s trademark star-spangled outfit that is still worn today.

articles.title: Texas' Arch Manning Compared to Giants' Jameis Winston by Former NFL Insider
articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning has drawn a unique comparison as he navigates through his 2026 campaign with the Longhorns.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning has drawn a unique comparison as he navigates through his 2026 campaign with the Longhorns.

A former NFL scouting director explained to On3.com's Pete Nakos why he believes that Manning shares a similarity with New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston.

"Not because of the exact players they are, but because for the one great play they make it comes with some hiccups," the former scouting director told Nakos.

Winston was selected with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 NFL draft following a stellar tenure at Florida State in which he earned Heisman Trophy honors and captured a national championship.

He's dealt with inconsistency throughout his NFL career, though.

Winston has averaged 227.9 passing yards per game across 113 total appearances, tossing 163 touchdowns compared to 118 interceptions. In five games with the Giants this year, he's completed 57.0 percent of his passes for 957 yards and seven touchdowns while getting picked off five times.

Manning entered his 2026 campaign with high expectations, but Texas has suffered two losses in its first six games. He's thrown for 1,295 yards and 11 touchdowns to go along with five interceptions.

The 22-year-old has particularly struggled with ball security as of late, getting picked off three times in his past three starts.

The Longhorns own a 1-2 record over that span.

articles.title: Bolton 1-5 Middlesbrough: Will Lankshear at the double as Kim Hellberg's Boro emphatically move top of the Championship
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton and Middlesbrough at the Toughsheet Community Stadium; two goals from Will Lankshear, one each from Aidan Morris and Amario Cozier-Duberry, plus a Lewis Brunt own goal send Boro top
articles.body:
Will Lankshear continued his electric start to life in a Boro shirt with two more goals taking him to 11 in the league and 13 in all competitions.

Aidan Morris and Amario Cozier-Duberry were also on target, while Lewis Brunt scored an unfortunate own goal.

Kim Hellberg's side move two points above Swansea, who travel to QPR on Saturday, and three above West Ham, who take on Southampton.

It was clear from the off Middlesbrough were out to get their business wrapped up early. They had a corner inside the first minute, their first chance inside two and after 13, they had the lead, when former Bolton loanee Cozier-Duberry squared for Morris to sweep in.

The shots kept flowing. Bolton goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu made three excellent saves in quick succession, but there was only so much he could do. And just after the half-hour, it was 2-0 when Lankshear struck after exquisite teamwork in the build-up.

Boro were dominating and added a third on 39 minutes, when Adilson Malanda rose to meet a corner from the right and headed onto the unfortunate Brunt, who could do nothing to prevent the ball crossing the line.

Through sheer determination, Bolton reduced the deficit at half-time, when Theo Bair hit a shot through a crowd and, for almost 20 minutes after the break, they did not allow Boro a single shot.

However, much like the first half, Bazunu made another couple of saves - then the visitors added the gloss.

Cozier-Duberry first fired high into the net after being picked out by Riley McGree, before Lankshear struck the fifth of the night rolling in McGree's unselfish square ball after a lethal breakaway.

The key moments from the Toughsheet Community Stadium...

2: CLOSE ! Tommy Conway pokes just wide o of the far post with Will Lankshear to his right.

13: CHANCE ! Ruben Rodrigues has a golden chance to put Bolton in front, but his shot lacks pace and is easily held.

13: GOAL ! Less than 30 seconds later, Aidan Morris rolls home to give Middlesbrough the lead.

31: GOAL ! After some brilliant build-up, Conway puts the ball on a plate for Lankshear to tuck away his first of the night.

39: GOAL ! Adilson Malanda gets on the end of a corner from the right and heads onto Lewis Brunt, who can't stop the ball hitting his own net.

45+2: GOAL ! With almost the final kick of the first half, Theo Bair stays composed after chaos in the box to pull one back for Bolton.

65: SAVE ! Gavin Bazunu makes a stunning fingertip save to keep out a drive from distance.

70: CLOSE ! Max Conway drills into the side netting as the Bolton threat increases.

73: GOAL ! Cozier-Duberry collects a pass from Riley McGree and fires high into the net against his former club.

78: GOAL ! Lankshear adds the gloss after McGree unselfishly squares after a rapid breakaway.

How does Lankshear's start compare to Mitrovic's in record 2021/22 season?

Aleksandar Mitrovic starred in the second tier in 2021/22, when he scored a Championship-record 43 on the way to winning the title with Fulham.

And Lankshear's start is not a million miles away from the one the Serb made.

Mitrovic had taken 22 more touches in the opposition box, hit 10 more shots and scored one more goal at this point.

However, taking into account non-penalty goals only, the pair are level.

How many goals will Lankshear score this season? Have your say below...

Schumacher: Even at our best it would've been tough

Bolton 's Steven Schumacher speaking to Sky Sports:

"The way Middlesbrough performed tonight, even if we were at our very, very best, it would've been a tough night for us because of the quality they've got and (the fact) they were at it.

"I'm pleased with some aspects of the way we played. We created some really good chances at times, but the gulf between the teams at this moment was evident. They were a lot more clinical than what we were and showed why they are a real top team.

"It's a tough one to take, but it's something to learn from."

Hellberg: Not keeping a clean sheet doesn't matter too much when you score five!

Middlesbrough 's Kim Hellberg speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's absolutely up there, especially when you look at the team we played, who drew with Southampton and beat Wolves away. They are a very good team and a brave team we played against and we were at our best.

"We used the space behind the last line, which we did very, very well, then we played fluid football, which we are able to do.

"You know the crowd has almost given up when you go 3-0 up, but then they score that goal and that makes it a little bit tougher. You know the crowd are going to go quite hard at it in the first 15 minutes (of the second half) and the players are too.

"But we managed that in a very good way, didn't concede many chances. Of course you want to keep the clean sheet, but if you score five, it doesn't matter that much."

articles.title: Quique Sánchez Flores: "Un partido así no lo hemos hecho en todo el curso, nos vamos enfadados"
articles.standfirst: El técnico lamentó que la reacción del último cuarto de hora no se hubiese producido mucho antes
articles.summary: El técnico lamentó que la reacción del último cuarto de hora no se hubiese producido mucho antes
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores no ocultó su enfado al término del encuentro ante el Málaga después de que el Alavés firmara probablemente su peor partido desde que está en el banquillo de Mendizorroza. El técnico madrileño fue muy crítico con la gestión de sus jugadores con el balón y lamentó que la reacción del último cuarto de hora no se hubiese producido mucho antes. Análisis: "No hemos jugado el partido que queríamos. Hemos entrado bien, pero hemos acumulado demasiadas perdidas y eso ha supuesto un contagio general. Ha habido demasiado estrés a la hora de jugar el balón. En el primer tiempo hemos estado alejadísimos de lo que hubiésemos imaginado. Hemos cambiado el sistema en el segundo tiempo, pero no nos hemos encontrado hasta los últimos 15 minutos". El peor partido de la temporada: "Un partido así no lo hemos hecho en toda la temporada. Es el primer partido en el que no nos hemos encontrado en ningún momento, hemos estado incómodos y erráticos. Lo sentimos por la afición por no darle el partido que queríamos, pero voy a estar más que nunca con los jugadores porque ahora es el momento de estar con ellos". Demasiados errores: "Esa forma de desaparecer del partido a base de agrandar la figura del rival sabemos todos cómo funciona. Cuando un equipo empieza a cometer errores y se siente mal, sin que el rival nos haya generado nada, éramos merecedores de irnos por detrás por el partido que estábamos haciendo. A los jugadores les ha costado encontrar la situación de poder generar fútbol y situaciones". Ocasión desaprovechada: "Lo de respetar al rival lo tenemos muy claro. En nuestros mejores días podemos ganar al Real Madrid y al Málaga. En nuestros peores días podemos perder con el Málaga y vamos a perder con los grandes. Ha sido un muy mal día en el que rescatamos los últimos 15 minutos. En partidos así estamos expuestos a perder contra cualquiera". Dinámica negativa: "Los resultados dan y quitan confianza. Partidos como el de hoy nos arrastran confianza. Durante la semana hemos sido conscientes de que el partido era muy importante y de cómo teníamos que salir, pero sólo nos ha durado cinco minutos y a partir de ahí hemos empezado a fallar pases. Lo único bueno es que el Málaga no nos ha generado demasiadas ocasiones para todas las facilidades. Estamos enfadados todos". Preocupación: "No me voy preocupado, me voy enfadado como todos los jugadores. Hemos entregado un montón de cosas que no estamos acostumbrados a entregar. Se nos ha ido el tiempo sin hacer lo que queríamos hacer".

articles.title: Xabi Alonso y su salida del Madrid: "Acabó antes de lo previsto y sin saber si iba a terminar bien o mal..."
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Chelsea se sincera sobre su salida del Real Madrid el curso pasado
articles.summary: El técnico del Chelsea se sincera sobre su salida del Real Madrid el curso pasado
articles.body: Xabi Alonso tiene la misión de devolver al Chelsea a lo más alto de la Premier League. El entrenador español, en su primera temporada en Stamford Bridge, está dejando buenas sensaciones y olvidando poco a poco la decepción de su etapa en el Real Madrid. En una entrevista con Jamie Carragher, el exentrenador madridista repasa su etapa en el conjunto blanco y se sincera sobre su salida. "Me queda la sensación de que terminó un poco antes de lo previsto, sin saber si iba a terminar bien o mal. Fue a mitad de temporada, cuando todavía estábamos en La Liga, en la Champions League, así que...", lamenta Xabi. Su mirada atrás no tiene rencor hacia el conjunto madridista: "Es una experiencia dirigir en Madrid. Madrid es especial en todo. Es un poco diferente a otros clubes en todo. Y aprendí de eso, y no miro hacia atrás con enfado, miro hacia atrás y pienso: bueno, lo intenté, intenté dar lo mejor de mí". Xabi también habló en su entrevista en SkySports sobre su llegada al Chelsea y su plan para reverdecer los laureles del conjunto blue: "No tenía ninguna relación con el Chelsea, pero con el potencial que había aquí, algunas cosas podían cambiar y pensé que podíamos comenzar este camino juntos". Sobre la decisión de firmar con el Chelsea, dijo: "Se trataba del momento oportuno. Para mí, era el momento adecuado después del Leverkusen. Después del Madrid, tuve tiempo libre y quería tener esa buena sensación, esa buena conexión sobre adónde ir".

articles.title: Funes: "Hay una falta clara en el gol del Alavés"
articles.standfirst: El técnico malaguista se quejó del arbitraje en Mendizorroza
articles.summary: El técnico malaguista se quejó del arbitraje en Mendizorroza
articles.body: El Málaga se marchó de Mendizorroza con un punto que supo a poco después de dejar escapar la victoria en el tramo final. Adrián Niño adelantó a los blanquiazules al borde del descanso, pero Aitor Mañas igualó en el minuto 89 tras un rechace en el área. Funes terminó especialmente molesto con la acción del empate y señaló directamente al arbitraje. "Hay una falta clara en el gol del Alavés", dijo “Vemos que, en su gol, pisa claramente a Recio”, denunció el técnico granadino durante su comparecencia ante los medios. Funes consideró que el tanto del Alavés estuvo precedido por una falta sobre el centrocampista malaguista y no ocultó su malestar por una acción que terminó resultando decisiva para el resultado. El entrenador del Málaga lamentó que su equipo no pudiera llevarse una victoria que, a su juicio, había merecido por el rendimiento ofrecido durante buena parte del encuentro. “Estoy insatisfecho por nuestra gente, por no poder darles esa victoria que hemos rozado. También por los jugadores, que han hecho un gran esfuerzo y un gran partido”, explicó. Funes fue más allá al valorar el partido y calificó la primera mitad como “la mejor primera parte de la temporada”, además de considerar que fue “el mejor partido a domicilio” del curso. El técnico también destacó que el equipo supo corregir uno de los problemas que le habían castigado en jornadas anteriores: las transiciones del rival. “Hemos estado más juntos hoy y eso nos ha hecho recuperar más balones y hacer transiciones”, señaló. Pese al empate, Funes quiso quedarse con las sensaciones y con la evolución mostrada por el Málaga. “Hemos estado en la línea que queríamos”, afirmó. El conjunto blanquiazul continúa sin ganar, pero el entrenador considera que el rendimiento mostrado en Vitoria puede servir como punto de apoyo para lo que viene.

articles.summary: Te contamos los detalles para que puedas disfrutar del encuentro correspondiente a la jornada 10
articles.body: Racing de Santander y Espanyol se enfrentan en un partido correspondiente a la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports. El encuentro se disputa este sábado 24 de octubre a las 16.15 horas en el estadio de El Sardinero. Será un partido en el que los dos equipos tratarán de poner fin al mal momento por el que atraviesan. El Racing de Santander lleva cuatro partidos en el campeonato sin lograr la victoria. Una mala racha en la que sólo ha sumado un punto de 12 posibles. Los cántabros perdieron ante Barcelona, Celta y Osasuna y empataron contra el Valencia. En la misma situación se encuentra el Espanyol. Los pericos tampoco han sido capaces de ganar en sus cuatro últimos compromisos y también han sumado solo un punto. En su caso, perdieron contra Rayo Vallecano, Elche y Atlético y empataron frente al Málaga. El partido entre Racing de Santander y Espanyol se juega este sábado 24 de octubre a las 16.15 horas. El partido entre Racing de Santander y Espanyol de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de DAZN. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el vídeo con el resumen de las mejores jugadas y los goles. El Racing de Santander, con ocho puntos en la clasificación, llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Espanyol tras perder (2-0) con Osasuna la pasada jornada. El Espanyol, con ocho puntos en la clasificación, llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Racing de Santander tras perder (0-1) con el Atlético la pasada jornada.

articles.title: Ipswich's Issa Diop escaped a red card for a foul on Nottingham Forest's James McAtee - but was it the right call?
articles.summary: Ipswich's Issa Diop was shown a yellow card for a last-man foul on James McAtee when it was deemed he didn't deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by referee Thomas Bramall after a VAR intervention; Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said it was a 'clear red card' after the 1-1 draw
articles.body:
With less than five minutes of the second half played when Diop slid in on Forest's James McAtee, a sending off could have transformed the outcome of the game.

Glasner was adamant Diop had denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity. But Diop himself told Sky Sports he was "quite confident" he would stay on the field as the officials and VAR came to their decision.

There was also split opinion among the Sky Sports pundits, too.

On co-commentary, Lee Hendrie reckoned Diop was "really lucky" and criticised the reasoning from the referee. Post-match, Ashley Young defended the decision.

Here we break down the key moment - and ask you to have your say.

Ipswich centre-back Diop slid in on McAtee, missing the ball and making contact with the Forest player as he tried to break through on goal.

Ref Thomas Bramall didn't blow his whistle but was then advised by VAR to go to the pitchside monitor to review the incident "for a possible denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity".

After watching replays, ref Bramall announced it was a foul and then said: "However, because the player knocks it to the right side of the goal, the final decision is direct free-kick and a yellow card to No.6."

In his announcement, Bramall indicates that McAtee's touch before he is fouled by Diop means the situation cannot be deemed as an "obvious goal-scoring opportunity".

McAtee touches the ball forwards. That takes the ball into the box and slightly to the right.

Significantly to the right? "I do not think he has touched it away from goal at all," said Hendrie on Sky Sports commentary.

Glasner later argued that moving the ball to the right would have increased the possibility for McAtee to score.

"When you run against the keeper and you run straight, often the angle is not really good, so we are telling the players to sometimes create an angle and I think he prepared his finish by going a little bit half-right, so the keeper has to move and opens the near or far post."

But it seems there were other factors on Bramall's mind, too.

Soon after the incident, the Premier League Match Centre posted an explanation on social media of what had happened, including both the on-field announcement from Bramall but also a sentence he said during the decision-making process.

"It's a heavy touch, with the defender inside and he knocks the ball away from the goal - I'm going to go direct free-kick and yellow card".

Bramall didn't mention the "heavy touch" in his announcement at Portman Road - but was McAtee ever actually going to reach the ball after he knocked it forwards? Leif Davis was the Ipswich defender "inside" the ref is referring to.

"McAtee isn't going to get there before Davis. He's quick," said Ashley Young on Sky Sports . "Plus, the ball is going through to the goalkeeper. I think the goalkeeper is going to get there as well.

Diop also used Davis' presence in his defence. "I did the tackle because I saw Leif coming and covering and also he pushed the ball wide and too far."

"The red card will split decision," said former Forest boss Steve Cooper afterwards on Sky Sports.

"Forest fans and staff and players will feel hard done by but if it had gone against Ipswich, they would definitely have felt hard done by."

There was even division on whether it was right for Bramall to wait for VAR to intervene, with Gibbs-White and Cooper critical of the ref for not making the decision initially, while Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil praised the process.

A controversial way to kick off the Premier League weekend. Have your say on the incident in our poll above!

articles.title: Xavi Espart backed to handle Yan Diomande in El Clasico
articles.summary: The youngster’s former coach is confident in his ability.
articles.body:
Xavi Espart is being tipped to shine if he comes up against Yan Diomande in Sunday's clash between Barcelona and Real Madrid in La Liga.

The youngster has been a revelation so far this season, starring at both left-back and right-back for Barcelona. He also heads into the game after scoring his first Champions League goal against PSG in midweek.

Espart's former La Masia coach Pau Moral says he has no doubts that the defender will come good once again at the weekend but warned that fans must realise he's not the finished article yet.

"I don't think he'll have any trouble defending against Diomande; he's a very intelligent player," he told Cadena SER. "We also have to be prepared for him to make mistakes someday. It's not normal for these La Masia lads to never make a single error."
